definition_en: a general idea separated from particular things, or the act of separating such an idea
core_image: 一间屋子里堆满具体的水果，墙上只挂着一张没有颜色的轮廓，所有差别都被抽走。
scene: 教室里，学生把具体的红苹果、青苹果逐一收进篮子，黑板上只留下一个没有颜色的轮廓。The students move from particular apples to a single outline, an abstraction they can discuss without holding any fruit.
sceneCN: 这里 abstraction 指「从具体事物中抽出的普遍观念」（第 1 个义项：与个别实例分离的一般观念）；句意为学生把一个个具体苹果收进篮子，黑板上只剩一个可讨论的轮廓。可辨识物件：果篮、黑板、粉笔、轮廓线。

senses.title: A general idea apart from particulars
senses.titleCN: 脱离具体事物的普遍观念
senses.definition: a general idea formed by separating what many particular things share from the things themselves
senses.definitionCN: 把许多具体事物共有的部分从事物本身分离出来而形成的一般观念
senses.example: Freedom is an abstraction until a specific person is denied it.
senses.exampleCN: 在某个具体的人被剥夺自由之前，自由只是一个抽象概念。
senses.why: The word is built from a verb meaning to draw away, so the idea has been pulled off the objects that first carried it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由表示「抽走」的动词构成，观念因此是从最初承载它的实物上被拉下来的。

senses.title: The act of pulling out a shared feature
senses.titleCN: 把共同特征抽离出来的动作
senses.definition: the process of noticing a feature shared by many cases and treating it as a separate object of thought
senses.definitionCN: 发现许多情形共有的特征、并把它当作独立思考对象的过程
senses.example: Her abstraction of the pattern took weeks of sorting.
senses.exampleCN: 她把这一规律抽象出来，花了数周时间整理。
senses.why: The noun ending marks an action rather than a thing, so this sense names the pulling-out itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词后缀标示的是动作而非实物，因此这一义项指的是抽离这件事本身。

senses.title: The quality of being abstract
senses.definition: the degree to which something is removed from direct depiction of concrete things
senses.definitionCN: 某物远离对具体事物的直接描绘的程度
senses.example: The sculpture's abstraction makes its subject hard to name.
senses.exampleCN: 这座雕塑的抽象性让人难以说出它表现的是什么。
senses.why: Once abstract things exist, the quality they share can be named with the same noun, a common shift from act to state.
senses.whyCN: 抽象事物一旦存在，它们共有的一种性质也用同一个名词来指称，这是由动作转向状态的常见变化。

senses.title: An abstract work of art
senses.definition: a painting or sculpture that does not aim to show recognizable objects
senses.definitionCN: 不以求表现可辨识物象为目标的绘画或雕塑
senses.example: The gallery hung three abstractions from the sixties.
senses.exampleCN: 画廊挂出了三件六十年代的抽象作品。
senses.why: Art criticism shortened the phrase abstract work to the noun itself, so a whole category of works took the name of its quality.
senses.whyCN: 艺术评论把「抽象作品」压缩成一个名词，于是整类作品直接用其性质来命名。

senses.title: A mind drawn away from the room
senses.definition: a condition in which someone's attention has left the present situation and turned inward
senses.definitionCN: 注意力离开眼前情境、转向内心的状态
senses.example: He nodded in abstraction while the kettle whistled.
senses.exampleCN: 水壶鸣响时，他正出着神，只是点了点头。
senses.why: The old sense of withdrawing the mind from the world survives in this phrase, where attention has been drawn elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 「把心思从外界抽回」的旧义保存在这个说法里，注意力正是被拉到了别处。

senses.title: A taking away of something
senses.definition: the removal of a substance or part from a place where it naturally belongs
senses.definitionCN: 把某种物质或部分从它原本所在之处取走
senses.example: The abstraction of water from the river lowered its level.
senses.exampleCN: 从河里抽水使水位下降了。
senses.why: This is the most literal physical reading: something is drawn away from its source, with no idea involved.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的物理读法：某物被从源头抽走，并不涉及观念。

senses.title: A simplified layer that hides detail
senses.titleCN: 隐藏细节的简化层（计算机用语）
senses.definition: a programming interface that presents a simple surface while concealing the complex machinery beneath
senses.definitionCN: 呈现简单接口、同时把下方复杂机制隐藏起来的编程界面
senses.example: The library offers an abstraction over the network calls.
senses.exampleCN: 这个库在网络调用之上提供了一层抽象。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the word because a layer, like a concept, leaves out the particular details that lie underneath.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用这个词，是因为一层接口就像概念一样，把底下的具体细节省略掉。

senses.title: Money taken for oneself
senses.definition: the wrongful taking of money or property entrusted to someone's care
senses.definitionCN: 不正当地取走交由某人保管的钱财
senses.example: The audit found an abstraction of funds from the trust.
senses.exampleCN: 审计发现有人从信托基金中挪用资金。
senses.why: Legal usage keeps the concrete sense of drawing something away, with the added charge that the taking was improper.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法保留「把东西抽走」的具体义，只额外加上「取走不正当」的指控。

intro.en: Abstraction comes from Latin abstractio, a noun of action from abstrahere, itself built from a prefix meaning away from and trahere, to draw or pull.
intro.cn: abstraction 来自拉丁名词 abstractio，是动词 abstrahere 的动作名词；该动词由表示「离开」的前缀与 trahere「拉、拖」构成。

items.en: Trahere meant to draw or pull and also gave tract, traction and contract. Its deeper origin is generally considered to lie in a reconstructed Indo-European root whose exact shape is not settled.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖」，还衍生出 tract、traction、contract。其更早来源一般认为是某个印欧语词根，但确切形态尚无定论。

items.en: A prefix meaning away from combined with trahere to make abstrahere, to draw away, and the action noun abstractio named that drawing off.
items.cn: 表示「离开」的前缀与 trahere 合成 abstrahere「抽走」，其动作名词 abstractio 指「抽离」这一行为。

items.en: The word entered English in the fourteenth century, at first naming a withdrawal of the mind from worldly matters rather than a general idea.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪进入英语，最初指心思从世俗事务中抽离，而非指一般观念。

items.en: By the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the word settled on the general idea separated from particulars, the sense that now leads everyday use.
items.cn: 到十六、十七世纪，这个词稳定为「从具体事物中分离出来的一般观念」，这一义项如今在日常使用中占主导。

items.en: Later technical uses split off: an abstraction layer in computing hides detail, while a legal abstraction names money taken from where it belongs.
items.cn: 后来技术用法又分出两支：计算机中的抽象层隐藏细节，法律上的抽象则指从应属之处取走钱财。

items.en: Source uncertain (first English citation and pre-Latin origin): the exact earliest record is not fixed, and the deeper root of trahere is a reconstructed form rather than a demonstrated one.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见书证与拉丁语之前的来源）：确切的最早记录并无定论，trahere 更早的词根属重构形式，而非已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds words built from the same Latin verb with different prefixes; group two holds near neighbours that name the product of abstract thinking.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁动词、但前缀不同的词；第二组是表示抽象思维产物的近义词。

entries.definition: The adjective and verb behind the noun: an abstract quality, or to take something out.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的形容词与动词：抽象的性质，或把某物抽出。

entries.definition: Built with a prefix meaning out of, so it stresses taking something out of a source rather than leaving detail behind.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「向外」的前缀构成，强调从来源中取出，而非省略细节。

entries.definition: Built with a prefix meaning under or away, used for taking a number away from another.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「在下、离开」的前缀构成，用于从一个数中减去另一个数。

entries.definition: Built with a prefix meaning toward, so it means drawing something closer rather than drawing an idea off.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「朝向」的前缀构成，意为把某物吸引过来，而非把观念抽离。

entries.definition: A general idea held in the mind; it names the result, while abstraction can also name the act of forming it.
entries.definitionCN: 头脑中持有的一般观念；它指结果，而 abstraction 也能指形成观念的动作。

entries.definition: A statement that applies a finding to many cases; it stresses the claim, not the removal of detail.
entries.definitionCN: 把某一发现推广到许多情形的说法；它强调论断本身，而非省略细节。

entries.definition: A vague or personal idea; it often suggests something less carefully formed than an abstraction.
entries.definitionCN: 模糊或个人的想法；常暗示它不如抽象概念那样经过仔细构造。

entries.definition: The plain word for something thought of; abstraction is the formal term for an idea stripped of particulars.
entries.definitionCN: 指所思之物的日常词；abstraction 是表示剥离具体细节后观念的正式说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real relatives and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: A prefix meaning away plus a verb meaning draw: to draw the shared part away from the cases.
normal.cn: 表示「离开」的前缀加表示「拉」的动词：把共有部分从各个实例中拉走。

normal.en: The family runs abstract, abstraction, abstractly, abstractness, abstractionism and abstractionist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 abstract、abstraction、abstractly、abstractness、abstractionism 与 abstractionist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the contrast between theory and practice: in the abstract, an abstraction from reality.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出理论与实践的对立：抽象地看、脱离现实的抽象。

normal.en: The same Latin verb appears in extract, subtract, attract and contract, each with a different prefix.
normal.cn: 同一个拉丁动词还出现在 extract、subtract、attract 与 contract 中，各自前缀不同。

normal.en: Computing says a layer is an abstraction because it shows a simple surface and hides the machinery.
normal.cn: 计算机领域说某一层是抽象，因为它只露出简单表面，把机器细节藏起来。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil sketch that keeps only the outline of a crowded market.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅铅笔速写，只留下拥挤市场的轮廓。

abstract.en: Picture a map that shows roads but erases every building.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只画道路、把所有建筑都擦掉的地图。

abstract.en: Picture a mask with two eye holes: the face is gone, but the way of seeing remains.
abstract.cn: 想象一副只有两个眼孔的面具：脸不见了，看的方式却留了下来。

examples.en: Children learn the abstraction of number before they can name it.
examples.cn: 儿童先掌握数的抽象概念，之后才能说出它。

examples.en: The diagram is an abstraction that leaves out every detail smaller than a street.
examples.cn: 这张图是一种抽象，凡小于街道的细节都被省略。

examples.en: His abstraction during dinner made the story seem addressed to someone else.
examples.cn: 他吃饭时心不在焉，让那番话像是在对别人说。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把共同点从一堆具体东西里「拉走」，只留下没有颜色的骨架 → 抽象

root: 拉丁 abstrahere「抽走」= 表示「离开」的前缀 + trahere「拉、拖」，动作名词 abstractio；trahere 更早来源属重构形式。英语 abstraction。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one move: a shared feature is pulled off the things that carry it, and the result then stands for ideas, art, absent minds, removed objects, hidden code and hidden money.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：共有特征从承载它的实物上被抽走，其结果随后用来指观念、艺术、出神的心思、被取走的物件、被隐藏的代码与被挪用的钱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy colored object reduced to a single outline hanging on a wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件有颜色有重量的实物被压缩成挂在墙上的单线轮廓。

branches.en: GENERAL IDEA: the outline survives without any of the fruit that produced it.
branches.cn: 普遍观念：轮廓留了下来，产生它的果子却全被拿开。

branches.en: THE ACT: the pulling out is itself something one can name and discuss.
branches.cn: 动作本身：抽离的过程也可以被命名、被讨论。

branches.en: QUALITY AND WORK: a surface can be abstract, and so can the object made from it.
branches.cn: 性质与作品：画面可以抽象，由画面制成的作品也可以抽象。

branches.en: DRAWN AWAY: the mind leaves the room, and an object leaves its place.
branches.cn: 被抽走：心思离开房间，物件离开原位。

branches.en: HIDDEN LAYER AND HIDDEN MONEY: one hides complexity, the other hides a taking.
branches.cn: 隐藏层与隐蔽的钱：一个藏起复杂，一个藏起取走。

intro.en: Abstraction is a Latin noun of action built from a prefix and a verb root, and both parts also build other English words.
intro.cn: abstraction 是由前缀与动词词根构成的拉丁动作名词，这两部分还构成其他英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere supplies abstract, extract, subtract, attract and contract; the prefix meaning away from narrows the family further.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 trahere 提供 abstract、extract、subtract、attract 与 contract；表示「离开」的前缀又进一步收窄了这个词族。

items.example: The prefix marks a movement away from a starting point.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出从起点离开的动作。

items.example: The root carries the physical sense of pulling.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带有「拉」的具体动作义。

items.meaning: to take out; existing only as an idea
items.meaningCN: 提取；只作为观念存在的
items.example: The summary abstracts the main claim.
items.exampleCN: 这份摘要把主要论点提取出来。

items.meaning: the act or result of drawing away
items.example: The abstraction took years to formulate.
items.exampleCN: 这个抽象概念花了多年才成形。

items.meaning: an art movement favouring abstract forms
items.meaningCN: 偏好抽象形式的艺术主张
items.example: Abstractionism dominated the gallery for a decade.
items.exampleCN: 抽象主义在这家画廊主导了十年。

items.meaning: an artist or supporter of abstract art
items.meaningCN: 抽象艺术的创作者或支持者
items.example: The abstractionist refused to paint a recognizable face.
items.exampleCN: 这位抽象派画家拒绝画出可辨认的脸。

items.example: The problem was discussed abstractly, with no names.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题被抽象地讨论，没有提到任何具体名字。

items.example: The abstractness of the film divided its audience.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片的抽象性使观众分成两派。

items.example: She gave an abstracted answer and kept staring out.
items.exampleCN: 她答得心不在焉，一直望着窗外。

definition_zh: 分类；归类过程；分类体系；范畴化；（数据）分类
definition_en: the act or result of sorting things into groups that share a feature
core_image: 长桌上散落着形状各异的零件，几只贴着不同标记的盒子把它们一排排收进去，桌面逐渐空出来。
scene: 仓库管理员把散落一地的零件按形状分放进不同颜色的收纳箱，箱盖贴着写好的标签。Careful categorization turns a heap of parts into shelves that anyone can search.
sceneCN: 这里 categorization 指「把事物按共同特征分门别类的过程」（第 1 个义项：按共有特征划分并归入类别的动作）；句意为仔细的分类把一堆零件变成人人可查的货架。可辨识物件：零件、收纳箱、标签、货架。

pos.zh: 分类；归类过程；分类体系；范畴化；（数据）分类

senses.title: The act of sorting into groups
senses.titleCN: 按共同特征分门别类的动作
senses.definition: the act of placing things into groups according to features they share
senses.definitionCN: 按照事物共有的特征把它们放进不同组别的动作
senses.example: Categorization begins when someone asks which features matter.
senses.exampleCN: 分类始于有人提出「哪些特征才算数」这一问题。
senses.why: The noun names the carrying out of the verb: deciding that this item belongs with that group.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指动词所表示的动作的实施：判定此物属于彼类。

senses.title: A resulting set of classes
senses.definition: the arrangement of groups produced by sorting, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 分类之后形成的各组安排，作为整体来看待
senses.example: The report's categorization put the storms into three strength bands.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告的分类把风暴归入三个强度等级。
senses.why: An action noun can also name its product, so the same word covers both the sorting and the shelf of groups left behind.
senses.whyCN: 动作名词也能指动作的产物，因此同一个词既指分类过程，也指分好后留下的一整套组别。

senses.title: Mental grouping in the mind
senses.definition: the mental process by which people group similar experiences and treat them as one kind
senses.definitionCN: 人们把相似经验归在一起、当作同一类来处理的心理过程
senses.example: Infants rely on categorization to make sense of a noisy room.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿依靠范畴化才能在嘈杂的房间里理出头绪。
senses.why: Psychology borrowed the everyday word because the mind sorts experience much as a clerk sorts stock.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借用这个日常词，因为心智整理经验的方式，就像管理员整理库存一样。

senses.title: Assigning words to grammatical classes
senses.definition: the analysis by which a word or construction is assigned to a grammatical class
senses.definitionCN: 把一个词或结构归入某一语法类别的分析
senses.example: Linguists study the categorization of verbs into transitive and intransitive classes.
senses.exampleCN: 语言学家研究动词如何被归入及物与不及物两类。
senses.why: Grammar is a system of classes, so placing a form in one of them is naturally called by the same name.
senses.whyCN: 语法本身就是一套类别系统，把一个形式放进其中某一类，自然也用同一个词来称呼。

senses.title: Sorting data into labelled classes
senses.titleCN: 把数据归入带标签的类别
senses.definition: the assignment of records, images or texts to predefined classes by rules or by a trained model
senses.definitionCN: 按规则或用训练过的模型把记录、图像或文本指派到预先设定的类别
senses.example: Automatic categorization filed every complaint by topic overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 自动分类在一夜之间按主题归档了所有投诉。
senses.why: Machine learning extends the clerk's task to a machine: each item still goes into a box chosen by shared features.
senses.whyCN: 机器学习把管理员的工作延伸到机器：每一项仍然按共有特征放进某个盒子。

senses.title: An official classification scheme
senses.definition: an established scheme that assigns jobs, books, species or records to fixed classes
senses.definitionCN: 把职位、图书、物种或档案指派到固定类别的既定方案
senses.example: The library's categorization follows subject rather than author.
senses.exampleCN: 这家图书馆的分类按学科而不是按作者。
senses.why: Institutions need stable shelves, so the word comes to name the written scheme as well as the act of using it.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要稳定的架子，因此这个词既指使用方案的动作，也指写下来的方案本身。

senses.title: Putting people into simplified boxes
senses.definition: the habit of treating a person mainly as a member of a broad group, often losing individual detail
senses.definitionCN: 主要按某个宽泛群体来对待一个人、因而丢掉个体细节的习惯
senses.example: Categorization by accent often hides differences inside a group.
senses.exampleCN: 按口音归类常常掩盖了群体内部的差异。
senses.why: The same sorting gesture turns harmful when the box replaces the person instead of merely describing one feature.
senses.whyCN: 当盒子取代了人本身、而不只是描述某一特征时，同样的分类动作就变得有害。

senses.title: Grouping organisms in taxonomy
senses.titleCN: 生物分类学中的类群划分
senses.definition: the placement of organisms into taxonomic groups on the basis of shared ancestry or form
senses.definitionCN: 依据共同祖先或形态把生物归入分类学类群
senses.example: The museum's categorization separates fossils by geological period.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的分类按地质年代把化石分开。
senses.why: Biology took the general word and gave it a formal rule: shared features must reflect real relationships, not mere resemblance.
senses.whyCN: 生物学采用这个通用词并赋予正式规则：共有特征必须反映真实亲缘关系，而不只是外表相似。

intro.en: Categorization is an English action noun built on category, which reaches back through Latin and French to a Greek word for a public statement or predicate.
intro.cn: categorization 是英语动作名词，建立在 category 之上；category 经拉丁语与法语可追溯到一个表示「公开陈述、谓语」的希腊词。

items.en: Greek katēgoria meant a public statement or accusation, built from kata, against or down, and agoreuein, to speak in public. The speaking root is generally connected with agora, an assembly.
items.cn: 希腊语 katēgoria 指公开陈述或指控，由表示「针对、向下」的成分与「在公共场合说话」的动词构成；说话这一词根一般被认为与「集会」有关。

items.en: Aristotle used the plural of this word for the classes of predication, and from that technical use the modern sense of a class or group developed.
items.cn: 亚里士多德用这个词的复数来指谓述的各类别，现代「类别、组别」义正是从这一专门用法发展而来。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek term as categoria; French catégorie and English category followed, with category recorded in English from the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 拉丁语借用该希腊词为 categoria；随后有法语 catégorie 与英语 category，category 在英语中的记录可追溯到十五世纪。

items.en: Category plus the verb suffix -ize produced categorize in the early eighteenth century, and the action noun categorization followed the verb.
items.cn: category 加动词后缀构成 categorize，出现于十八世纪初；动作名词 categorization 随后由该动词派生。

items.en: Cognitive psychology, linguistics and computing each adopted the word in the twentieth century for their own sorting tasks.
items.cn: 认知心理学、语言学与计算机科学在二十世纪各自采用这个词，用来指本领域的分类工作。

items.en: Source uncertain (exact first dates and the pre-Greek origin of the speaking root): the earliest English record of the verb is not precisely fixed, and the deeper origin of agoreuein remains a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（确切首见年代与希腊语之前的相关来源）：该动词最早的英语记录没有精确年代，agoreuein 的更早来源仍属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same family that are easy to swap by mistake; group two holds other names for sorting.
note.cn: 第一组是同族中容易被误换的词；第二组是其他表示「分门别类」的词。

entries.definition: A class or group, not the act of sorting; the noun is the box, while categorization is the filling of boxes.
entries.definitionCN: 类别或组别本身，不是分类动作；名词指盒子，categorization 指往盒子里装。

entries.definition: The verb for performing the act; it takes an object, as in categorize the samples.
entries.definitionCN: 执行该动作的动词，可带宾语，如把这些样本归类。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning absolute or unconditional, as in a categorical denial; it is not a synonym for classified.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为绝对的、无条件的，如断然否认；它并不等于「已分类的」。

entries.definition: A list of items, from Greek katalogos, a counting or enrolment; it is a different compound from the category family.
entries.definitionCN: 物品清单，来自希腊语 katalogos「计数、登记」；与 category 词族是不同的复合词。

entries.definition: The broad word for arranging things in classes; categorization is close but often stresses the mental or automatic act.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物安排进类别的通用词；categorization 与之相近，但常强调心理或自动的动作。

entries.definition: The everyday word for putting things in order, often by hand; it need not create named classes.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西按顺序摆放的日常词，常指手工操作；不一定形成有名称的类别。

entries.definition: A formal system of named groups, especially in biology; it is the scheme, not the act of using it.
entries.definitionCN: 有名称的正式分类系统，尤用于生物学；它指方案本身，而非使用方案的动作。

entries.definition: The act of putting items together without necessarily giving each group a fixed label.
entries.definitionCN: 把项目放在一起的动作，不一定给每一组固定标签。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Greek source, the English family and the everyday sorting scenes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：希腊语来源、英语同族词与日常的分类场景。

normal.en: The old Greek word meant a public statement; Aristotle turned its plural into classes of predication.
normal.cn: 这个希腊旧词指公开陈述；亚里士多德把它的复数变成谓述的类别。

normal.en: The family runs category, categorize, categorization, categorical and categorically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 category、categorize、categorization、categorical 与 categorically。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: social categorization, automatic categorization, data categorization.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：社会范畴化、自动分类、数据分类。

normal.en: A library shelf is the clearest picture: the same book can go in only one subject box.
normal.cn: 图书馆书架是最清楚的画面：同一本书只能进一个学科盒子。

normal.en: The word names both the act of sorting and the scheme that results from it.
normal.cn: 这个词既指分类的动作，也指分类后得到的方案。

abstract.en: Picture a wardrobe divided by season, so every coat knows where to hang.
abstract.cn: 想象一个按季节分格的衣柜，每件外套都知道该挂哪里。

abstract.en: Picture a city map coloured by district, with no street drawn inside any block.
abstract.cn: 想象一张按城区上色的城市地图，每个色块内部都不画街道。

abstract.en: Picture a net whose knots decide which fish can pass and which cannot.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网，网眼大小决定了哪些鱼能过、哪些不能。

examples.en: Good categorization makes a messy archive usable without deleting anything.
examples.cn: 好的分类让杂乱的档案变得可用，却不必删掉任何东西。

examples.en: The study found that early categorization shapes how children remember new animals.
examples.cn: 研究发现，早期的范畴化会影响儿童如何记住新的动物。

examples.en: Her categorization of the evidence was challenged in court.
examples.cn: 她对证据的分类在法庭上受到质疑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把一堆东西按「像不像」分成几只盒子，盒子上再写名字 → 分类、范畴化

root: 希腊 katēgoria「公开陈述、谓语」= 表示「针对」的成分 + agoreuein「公开说话」（一般认为与 agora「集会」相关）；经拉丁 categoria、法语 catégorie 入英语为 category，再加动词后缀与动作名词后缀成 categorize、categorization。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: things are placed into boxes by shared features, and the same act is then read as a mental process, a grammar rule, a data pipeline, an official scheme, a social prejudice and a taxonomic method.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：事物按共有特征被放进不同盒子，这个动作随后被读作心理过程、语法规则、数据流程、官方方案、社会偏见与生物分类方法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowded table cleared into a few labelled boxes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张堆满东西的桌子被清空，物件进了几只贴标签的盒子。

branches.en: THE ACT: the hands do the sorting before any label exists.
branches.cn: 动作：标签尚未出现，手已经在分拣。

branches.en: THE SCHEME: once the boxes are named, the arrangement becomes a system others must follow.
branches.cn: 方案：盒子一旦有了名字，这套安排就成为别人必须遵循的制度。

branches.en: MIND AND MACHINE: both group by shared features, one with neurons and one with rules.
branches.cn: 心智与机器：两者都按共有特征分组，一个靠神经，一个靠规则。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: a word is sent to a class as surely as a part is sent to a bin.
branches.cn: 语法：词被送进某个类别，正如零件被送进某个箱子。

branches.en: TWO EDGES: the same box can flatten a person or clarify a fossil lineage.
branches.cn: 两端：同一个盒子既能压平一个人，也能理清一条化石谱系。

intro.en: Categorization is a chain of English building blocks laid on a Greek noun that Latin and French carried westward.
intro.cn: categorization 是一串英语构词成分叠加在一个希腊名词上，该名词经拉丁语与法语向西传播。

latinIntro.en: Latin categoria and Late Latin categoricus supply the base; the English verb and noun suffixes then extend the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 categoria 与晚期拉丁 categoricus 提供基础；英语的动词与名词后缀再把这个词族延伸开。

items.structure: Greek katēgoria through Latin categoria (class, predicate)
items.example: Each category has its own shelf.
items.exampleCN: 每个类别都有自己的架子。

items.example: The clerk categorizes each form by type.
items.exampleCN: 职员按类型把每份表格归类。

items.meaning: the act or result of classifying
items.example: The categorization took a full week.
items.exampleCN: 这次分类花了整整一周。

items.example: She gave a categorical answer.
items.exampleCN: 她给出了一个断然的答复。

items.example: He denied the claim categorically.
items.exampleCN: 他断然否认了这一说法。

items.meaning: one who or that which classifies
items.example: The categorizer sorts thousands of messages a minute.
items.exampleCN: 这个分类程序每分钟处理数千条信息。

items.meaning: a class inside a larger class
items.example: Jazz sits in a subcategory of music.
items.exampleCN: 爵士乐属于音乐之下的一个子类。

items.example: The archive had to recategorize the letters.
items.exampleCN: 档案馆不得不重新归类这些信件。

items.meaning: having been placed in a class
items.example: The files are categorized by year.
items.exampleCN: 这些文件按年份归类。

definition_zh: 把……归类；分门别类整理；判定为某一类；（计算机）自动分类
definition_en: to place something into a class or group according to its features
core_image: 一张张卡片被手指按颜色推进不同的抽屉，抽屉外面贴着写好的字样。
scene: 图书馆新到的书堆在推车上，管理员按主题把它们一本本插进不同的书架。Librarians categorize new arrivals by subject before they reach the shelf.
sceneCN: 这里 categorize 指「按特征把事物归入某一类别」（第 1 个义项：把某一项放进共有特征相同的组里）；句意为管理员在新书入架之前按学科把它们归类。可辨识物件：推车、书脊、书架、主题标签。

senses.title: Place an item in a class
senses.titleCN: 把某一项放进某个类别
senses.definition: to decide which class or group an item belongs to and put it there
senses.definitionCN: 判定某一项属于哪个类别或组别，并把它放进去
senses.example: Librarians categorize new arrivals by subject before they reach the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 管理员在新书入架之前按学科把它们归类。
senses.why: The verb is the doing of category: it takes a single item and gives it a home among others like it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词就是「做类别」：拿一个单项，为它在同类中安置一个位置。

senses.title: Sort a whole set into groups
senses.titleCN: 把一整批东西分门别类
senses.definition: to divide a collection into groups so that each group holds one kind
senses.definitionCN: 把一整批东西分开，使每一组只装一种
senses.example: She categorized the photographs by decade and then by place.
senses.exampleCN: 她先按年代、再按地点把照片分门别类。
senses.why: With a plural object the verb describes repeated placing, so the result is a sorted set rather than one assigned item.
senses.whyCN: 宾语为复数时，这个动词描述反复放置的动作，结果是一整套被分好的东西，而不是单项的归属。

senses.title: Judge something to be of a type
senses.definition: to regard or label something as belonging to a particular kind, often with a judgement attached
senses.definitionCN: 把某物看作或标为属于某一特定种类，常带有判断色彩
senses.example: The reviewer categorized the film as a comedy, though it ends in grief.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者把这部电影归为喜剧，尽管它以悲痛收场。
senses.why: The phrase with as shifts the verb from moving an object to declaring its identity, a common pattern with verbs of naming.
senses.whyCN: 与表示「作为」的词连用时，动词从搬运物件转为宣布其身份，这是命名类动词的常见模式。

senses.title: Sort data by machine
senses.definition: to assign records, images or messages to predefined classes by algorithm
senses.definitionCN: 用算法把记录、图像或信息指派到预先设定的类别
senses.example: The filter categorizes every email as work, family or junk.
senses.exampleCN: 过滤器把每封邮件归为工作、家庭或垃圾三类。
senses.why: Computing keeps the clerk's gesture but replaces the hand with a rule, so the verb needs no human subject.
senses.whyCN: 计算机保留了管理员的手势，却用规则代替了手，因此这个动词不必有人的主语。

senses.title: Group experiences in the mind
senses.titleCN: 在认知上把经验归为一类
senses.definition: to treat similar perceptions or memories as instances of one mental kind
senses.definitionCN: 把相似的知觉或记忆当作同一种心理类别中的实例
senses.example: The brain categorizes a new shape in less time than a blink.
senses.exampleCN: 大脑给一个新形状归类的时间比一次眨眼还短。
senses.why: The mind performs the same act invisibly, and the verb is used for it because the outcome is still a class.
senses.whyCN: 心智在看不见的地方做同样的动作，动词仍可用于它，因为结果同样是一个类别。

senses.title: Assign an organism to a taxon
senses.titleCN: 把生物归入某个分类单元
senses.definition: to place an organism or fossil into a taxonomic group on formal grounds
senses.definitionCN: 依据正式标准把生物或化石归入某个分类学类群
senses.example: The team categorized the fossil as an early reptile rather than an amphibian.
senses.exampleCN: 研究团队把这块化石归为早期爬行动物，而不是两栖动物。
senses.why: Taxonomy makes the everyday verb accountable: the box must be justified by shared ancestry or structure.
senses.whyCN: 分类学让这个日常动词负有责任：把东西放进哪个盒子，必须由共同祖先或结构来证明。

senses.title: Put a person into a narrow box
senses.titleCN: 把人简单化地归入某一类
senses.definition: to treat someone chiefly as a member of a broad social group, ignoring individual differences
senses.definitionCN: 主要把某人当作某个宽泛社会群体的成员，忽略个体差异
senses.example: It is unfair to categorize a student by a single test score.
senses.exampleCN: 凭一次考试分数就把一个学生归类是不公平的。
senses.why: The verb's neutral meaning turns critical here because the class replaces the person's particular case.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词的中性含义在这里带上了批评，因为类别取代了此人的具体情形。

senses.title: File records under headings
senses.definition: to store documents or accounts under fixed headings for later retrieval
senses.definitionCN: 把文件或账目按固定类目存放，以便日后检索
senses.example: The accountant categorized each receipt before closing the month.
senses.exampleCN: 会计在结账前把每张收据按类目归档。
senses.why: Filing is the practical form of the same act: an item is put where its kind is kept.
senses.whyCN: 归档是同一动作的实务形式：把一项放到它那一类该在的位置。

intro.en: Categorize is an English verb made from the noun category in the early eighteenth century, on the model of verbs ending in -ize.
intro.cn: categorize 是十八世纪初由名词 category 按动词后缀的构词模式造出的英语动词。

items.en: The Greek noun meant a public statement or accusation, from kata, against, and agoreuein, to speak publicly; the speaking root is generally linked to agora, an assembly.
items.cn: 这个希腊名词指公开陈述或指控，由表示「针对」的成分与「公开说话」的动词构成；说话词根一般被认为与「集会」有关。

items.en: Aristotle's use of its plural for classes of predication gave the word the sense of a class or group that it still carries.
items.cn: 亚里士多德用它指谓述的各类别，赋予这个词「类别、组别」的含义，这一含义沿用至今。

items.en: Latin categoria and French catégorie carried the noun into English as category in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 拉丁 categoria 与法语 catégorie 把这个名词带进英语，十五世纪时写作 category。

items.en: Category plus -ize produced categorize, first recorded in the early eighteenth century, at a time when many learned verbs were being coined this way.
items.cn: category 加动词后缀构成 categorize，最早记录于十八世纪初，当时许多学术动词正是这样造出。

items.en: The verb was later applied to machine sorting, memory research and social labelling, each adding a new object but not a new root.
items.cn: 这个动词后来被用于机器分类、记忆研究与社会标签，各义只添了新宾语，词根并未改变。

items.en: Source uncertain (exact first citation): the year in which the verb first appears in print is not firmly fixed, and earlier manuscript uses may exist that are not recorded in standard dictionaries.
items.cn: 来源不确定（确切首见书证）：该动词首次印行的年份没有定论，可能存在标准词典未收录的更早手稿用例。

note.en: Group one holds family members that differ in part of speech; group two holds other verbs for arranging things.
note.cn: 第一组是同族中词性不同的词；第二组是其他表示整理安排的动词。

entries.definition: The class itself; the verb needs an object, while the noun is the box the object goes into.
entries.definitionCN: 类别本身；动词需要宾语，而名词是宾语要进的盒子。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning unconditional, not the act of classifying; a categorical answer is a flat one.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为无条件的，并非分类动作；断然的答复就是毫不含糊的答复。

entries.definition: A standard for judging, from Greek krinein, to separate or decide; it is not built on the category root.
entries.definitionCN: 判断标准，来自希腊语 krinein「分开、判定」；并非建立在 category 的词根上。

entries.definition: A list or register of items, from a different Greek compound; cataloging records items, categorizing groups them.
entries.definitionCN: 物品清单或登记册，来自另一个希腊复合词；编目是登记项目，归类是分组。

entries.definition: To arrange in classes; it is close to categorize but more common in official and scientific settings.
entries.definitionCN: 安排进类别；与 categorize 相近，但更常用于官方与科学场合。

entries.definition: To arrange by some order; sorting may only sequence items, while categorizing creates groups.
entries.definitionCN: 按某种顺序排列；排序可能只是定次序，而归类会形成组别。

entries.definition: To attach a name to something; labelling is the visible sign of categorizing, not the grouping itself.
entries.definitionCN: 给某物贴上名称；贴标签是归类的可见标志，而非分组本身。

entries.definition: To bring items together; it need not imply that the group has a fixed name or rule.
entries.definitionCN: 把项目聚到一起；不一定意味着这一组有固定名称或规则。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the noun behind the verb, the suffix that makes it act, and the shelves it fills.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：动词背后的名词、使它成为动作的后缀，以及它填满的架子。

normal.en: The noun is category; the verb adds the suffix that means to make or place.
normal.cn: 名词是 category；动词加上表示「使成为、放置」的后缀。

normal.en: The family runs category, categorize, categorization, categorical and categorically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 category、categorize、categorization、categorical 与 categorically。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the objects it takes: categorize documents, categorize expenses, categorize responses.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示它能带哪些宾语：把文件分类、把支出分项、把答复归类。

normal.en: The pattern with as is a judgement: to categorize a film as a comedy is to declare its kind.
normal.cn: 与表示「作为」的词连用是一种判断：把电影归为喜剧，就是宣布它的种类。

normal.en: Machine learning uses the same verb for filters that sort mail without a person.
normal.cn: 机器学习用同一个动词来指无人参与的邮件分拣过滤器。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing one card into a drawer and closing it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一张卡片推进抽屉，然后关上。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf where every book faces the same way because its subject decided the place.
abstract.cn: 想象一个书架，每本书都朝同一方向，因为学科决定了位置。

abstract.en: Picture a filter that lets only one colour of sand through each hole.
abstract.cn: 想象一个筛子，每个孔只放行一种颜色的沙。

examples.en: The software can categorize thousands of images in an hour.
examples.cn: 这个软件一小时内能归类数千张图片。

examples.en: Do not categorize a whole neighbourhood by one incident.
examples.cn: 不要因一起事件就给整个街区定性。

examples.en: She categorized the letters by sender before answering any of them.
examples.cn: 她在回信之前先按寄件人把信件归类。

dict_mnemonic.text: 先有「类别」这个盒子，再把东西一件件放进去 → 归类

root: 希腊 katēgoria「公开陈述、谓语」经拉丁 categoria、法语 catégorie 入英语为 category；category 加动词后缀 -ize 成 categorize。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hand: an item is sent to the box that matches its features, whether the hand is a clerk's, a mind's, a machine's or a taxonomist's.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一只手展开：某一项被送进与它特征相符的盒子，无论这只手属于职员、心智、机器还是分类学家。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a card sliding into a drawer whose label was decided before the card arrived.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张卡片滑进抽屉，抽屉上的标签在卡片到来之前就已写好。

branches.en: ONE ITEM: the verb starts with a single thing looking for its shelf.
branches.cn: 单项：动词从一件寻找自己架子的东西开始。

branches.en: THE WHOLE SET: repeated placing turns a heap into an order that can be searched later.
branches.cn: 整批：反复放置把一堆东西变成日后可查的次序。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT: saying what kind something is can be a verdict, not a harmless move.
branches.cn: 判断：宣布某物属于哪一类，可能是一项裁决，而非无害的搬动。

branches.en: WITHOUT A HAND: rules and neurons perform the same match at different speeds.
branches.cn: 无需人手：规则与神经元以不同速度完成同样的匹配。

branches.en: TWO BOXES: one must answer to ancestry, the other can flatten a person.
branches.cn: 两种盒子：一种必须对亲缘关系负责，另一种可能压平一个人。

intro.en: Categorize is a noun turned into a verb by a suffix, and the whole family can be read from its Greek base.
intro.cn: categorize 是由名词加后缀变成的动词，整个词族都可以从它的希腊语基础读起。

latinIntro.en: Latin categoria carries the Greek noun; English suffixes then build the verb, the action noun and the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 categoria 承载这个希腊名词；英语后缀随后造出动词、动作名词与形容词。

items.example: Each category has a colour.
items.exampleCN: 每个类别有一种颜色。

items.example: They categorize the samples by size.
items.exampleCN: 他们按大小把样本归类。

items.meaning: the act or result of classifying
items.example: Categorization made the archive usable.
items.exampleCN: 分类让档案变得可用。

items.example: The denial was categorical.
items.exampleCN: 这一否认毫不含糊。

items.example: She refused categorically.
items.exampleCN: 她断然拒绝了。

items.example: The categorizer never sleeps.
items.exampleCN: 这个分类程序从不休息。

items.example: Folk sits in a subcategory.
items.exampleCN: 民谣属于一个子类。

items.example: The editor recategorized the notes.
items.exampleCN: 编辑重新归类了这些笔记。

items.example: Categorizing takes longer than reading.
items.exampleCN: 归类比阅读更花时间。

derivatives.meaning: having been placed in a class

definition_zh: 心理表征；心理意象；概念结构；记忆痕迹；语义表征
definition_en: an internal stand-in in the mind for something outside it, such as an object, a scene or a meaning
core_image: 头脑里挂着一张透明地图，用不同形状的标记代替真实街道，却仍能指路。
scene: 闭眼之后，那个人仍能在脑中看见自家厨房的布置，连碗柜把手的位置都清楚。Even with eyes closed, she can inspect her kitchen through a mental representation built from years of use.
sceneCN: 这里 mental representation 指「头脑中替代外部事物的内部表征」（第 1 个义项：在心中为外部对象建立的替代性结构）；句意为她闭着眼也能凭多年使用形成的心理表征查看厨房。可辨识物件：闭眼的人、厨房轮廓、碗柜、把手标记。

pos.zh: 心理表征；心理意象；概念结构；记忆痕迹

collocations.zh: 对某一物体的心理表征

forms.label: 形容词（表征的；代表性的）

senses.title: An internal stand-in for something
senses.titleCN: 替代外部事物的内部结构
senses.definition: a structure in the mind that stands for an object, scene or state of affairs and allows it to be thought about
senses.definitionCN: 头脑中替代某一物体、场景或事态的结构，使人能够思考该对象
senses.example: Even with eyes closed, she can inspect her kitchen through a mental representation built from years of use.
senses.exampleCN: 即使闭着眼，她也能凭多年使用形成的心理表征查看厨房。
senses.why: The phrase says exactly what it does: a representation is something that stands in for another thing, and mental locates the stand-in inside the mind.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语字面就说清了它的作用：表征是替另一事物站出来的东西，而「心理的」限定这个替身位于头脑之内。

senses.title: A picture-like image in the mind
senses.titleCN: 头脑中类似图画的意象
senses.definition: a representation that has a visual or spatial form, as when someone turns a described room into an imagined picture
senses.definitionCN: 具有视觉或空间形式的表征，例如把人描述的房间变成想象中的画面
senses.example: She formed a mental representation of the room from his description.
senses.exampleCN: 她根据他的描述在脑中形成了那个房间的意象。
senses.why: The word image and the word representation overlap here: the mind keeps the shape of what it has seen or heard described.
senses.whyCN: 「意象」与「表征」在这里重叠：心智保留了所见或所听描述的形状。

senses.title: A structured concept
senses.definition: a representation made of linked features or rules rather than a picture, such as the concept of a bird
senses.definitionCN: 由相互关联的特征或规则构成、而非图画的表征，例如「鸟」这一概念
senses.example: The concept of a bird is a mental representation with feathers, wings and eggs linked inside it.
senses.exampleCN: 「鸟」这一概念是一种心理表征，内部把羽毛、翅膀与蛋联系起来。
senses.why: Thinking needs more than pictures: a concept holds relations, so the same phrase covers an abstract structure.
senses.whyCN: 思考不能只靠图画：概念要保存关系，因此同一个短语也涵盖抽象结构。

senses.title: A trace kept in memory
senses.definition: a stored representation that lets a past experience be recalled after the original event is gone
senses.definitionCN: 被储存起来的表征，使过去经验在原初事件消失后仍能被回忆
senses.example: The smell of chalk revived a mental representation of her first classroom.
senses.exampleCN: 粉笔的气味唤醒了她对第一间教室的心理表征。
senses.why: Memory is the keeping of a stand-in after the thing itself has left, which is precisely what a representation is.
senses.whyCN: 记忆就是在事物本身离开后仍保留一个替身，而这正是表征所做的事。

senses.title: The meaning side of language
senses.definition: the representation of meaning that a speaker attaches to a word or sentence
senses.definitionCN: 说话者赋予词或句子的意义表征
senses.example: Listeners build a mental representation of the sentence as the words arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 听众随着词语到来而逐步构建句子的心理表征。
senses.why: A sentence is not the meaning itself; the mind must construct a stand-in for what the words describe.
senses.whyCN: 句子并不等于意义本身；心智必须为词语所描述的内容构造一个替身。

senses.title: What the senses deliver
senses.definition: a representation formed from seeing, hearing or touching, before any name is attached
senses.definitionCN: 由看、听或触而形成、尚未附带名称的表征
senses.example: The visual mental representation of the face stayed with him longer than the name.
senses.exampleCN: 那张脸的视觉心理表征比名字在他脑中留得更久。
senses.why: Perception already selects and organizes input, so what arrives is a representation rather than the object itself.
senses.whyCN: 知觉已经在筛选与组织输入，因此到达心智的是表征，而非物体本身。

senses.title: A schema or working model
senses.definition: an organized representation that supplies expectations about how a familiar situation usually works
senses.definitionCN: 有组织的表征，为熟悉情境的通常运作方式提供预期
senses.example: Her mental representation of a restaurant told her to wait for a host.
senses.exampleCN: 她对餐馆的心理表征告诉她要先等领位员。
senses.why: A schema is a large representation with slots, so the phrase covers the model a person carries into a familiar scene.
senses.whyCN: 图式是一种带空位的大型表征，因此这个短语也涵盖人带进熟悉场景的心理模型。

senses.title: The content of a belief or desire
senses.definition: the proposition-like content that a belief, hope or fear is directed at
senses.definitionCN: 信念、希望或恐惧所指向的命题式内容
senses.example: Her hope rested on a mental representation of a house she had never seen.
senses.exampleCN: 她的希望寄托在对一栋从未见过的房子的心理表征上。
senses.why: Beliefs are about things even when those things are absent, and the phrase names what the mind is directed at.
senses.whyCN: 即使对象不在场，信念也总关于某物，而这个短语指的就是心智所指向的内容。

intro.en: The phrase joins mental, from Latin mens, mind, to representation, from Latin repraesentare, to bring before the eyes. It became a fixed term in philosophy and later in cognitive science.
intro.cn: 这个短语把来自拉丁 mens「心智」的 mental 与来自拉丁 repraesentare「呈现在眼前」的 representation 连在一起，先成为哲学术语，后成为认知科学术语。

items.en: Mens, with the stem ment-, meant mind, thought or intention. Its deeper origin is generally considered to belong to a reconstructed Indo-European root, but the exact pre-Latin form is not settled.
items.cn: mens（词干 ment-）意为心智、思想或意图。其更早来源一般认为是某个印欧语词根，但拉丁语之前的确切形态尚无定论。

items.en: The verb combined a prefix meaning again or back with praesentare, to present, itself from praesens, being before the eyes. It meant to bring something before someone, or to act in its place.
items.cn: 这个动词由表示「再次、向后」的前缀与 praesentare「呈现」构成，后者又来自 praesens「在眼前」，意为把某物带到某人面前，或代替它行动。

items.en: Mental entered English in the fifteenth century from Late Latin mentalis, and for a long time it named matters of the mind in general rather than images in particular.
items.cn: mental 在十五世纪经晚期拉丁 mentalis 进入英语，很长时间里泛指与心智有关的事，而非专指心中图像。

items.en: Representation came through French and named both the act of showing and the thing shown; the second sense made it useful for what stands in for an object.
items.cn: representation 经法语进入英语，既指展示的动作，也指被展示之物；后一义使它适合用来指替代某物的东西。

items.en: The full phrase became standard in philosophy of mind and in cognitive psychology in the twentieth century, when mental states were routinely described as representations of something.
items.cn: 整个短语在二十世纪的心智哲学与认知心理学中成为标准说法，当时人们习惯把心理状态描述为对某物的表征。

items.en: Source uncertain (first fixed use of the phrase): no single first citation is established for the exact collocation, and the deeper origin of mens is a reconstructed form rather than a demonstrated one.
items.cn: 来源不确定（该短语首次固定使用的时间）：这一确切搭配没有公认的最早书证；mens 的更早来源属重构形式，而非已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same two Latin families that are easy to confuse; group two holds other names for what the mind carries.
note.cn: 第一组是两个拉丁词族中容易混淆的词；第二组是心智所携带之物的其他名称。

entries.definition: Anything that stands for something else, from a picture to a legal claim; it needs mental only when the stand-in is in a mind.
entries.definitionCN: 任何替另一物站出来的东西，从图画到法律主张；只有替身位于头脑中时才需要加 mental。

entries.definition: Someone or something chosen to speak or stand for a larger group; it is a role, not a mental structure.
entries.definitionCN: 被选出来为更大群体发言或代表其的人或物；它指角色，不是心理结构。

entries.definition: Relating to the mind; it says where something happens, while the full phrase says what kind of structure is there.
entries.definitionCN: 与心智有关的；它说明事情发生在哪里，而整个短语说明那里存在何种结构。

entries.definition: A way of thinking characteristic of a person or group; it is a style of thought, not a stand-in for an object.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或群体特有的思维方式；它是思想风格，不是某物的替身。

entries.definition: A visual picture in the mind; it is one kind of mental representation, the kind that has spatial form.
entries.definitionCN: 头脑中的视觉画面；它是心理表征的一种，即具有空间形式的那一种。

entries.definition: A general idea built from shared features; a concept is a mental representation with a largely verbal structure.
entries.definitionCN: 由共有特征构成的一般观念；概念是一种以语词结构为主的心理表征。

entries.definition: A large mental frame with slots for the parts of a familiar situation; it is a schema, hence a kind of representation.
entries.definitionCN: 为熟悉情境的各部分留有位置的大型心理框架；它是图式，因而是表征的一种。

entries.definition: A simplified copy used to predict or explain; a mental model is a representation used for reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 用于预测或解释的简化副本；心理模型是用于推理的表征。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Latin sources, the cognitive science setting and the everyday act of picturing a room.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个拉丁来源、认知科学的语境，以及日常在脑中描绘房间的动作。

normal.en: Mental comes from the Latin word for mind; representation comes from a verb meaning to bring before the eyes.
normal.cn: mental 来自拉丁语中表示「心智」的词；representation 来自意为「带到眼前」的动词。

normal.en: A representation is a stand-in: it is not the thing, but it can be inspected in the thing's absence.
normal.cn: 表征是一个替身：它不是事物本身，却能在事物缺席时被查看。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: form a mental representation, a shared mental representation, a visual mental representation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：形成心理表征、共享的心理表征、视觉心理表征。

normal.en: The same noun appears in political representation and in representational art, where the stand-in is public rather than private.
normal.cn: 同一个名词也出现在政治代表与具象艺术中，那里的替身是公开的而非私人的。

normal.en: Cognitive science uses the phrase for concepts, memories and the meanings listeners build from sentences.
normal.cn: 认知科学用这个短语指概念、记忆以及听者从句子中构建的意义。

abstract.en: Picture a transparent map folded inside a pocket, useful only while it stays folded.
abstract.cn: 想象一张透明地图折在口袋里，只有折着的时候才有用。

abstract.en: Picture a theatre model of a city, complete enough to walk through with a finger.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市舞台模型，完整得可以用手指走一遍。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow that keeps the shape of a person after the person has left.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人离开后，影子仍保留他的形状。

examples.en: Two people can hold different mental representations of the same agreement.
examples.cn: 两个人可能对同一份协议持有不同的心理表征。

examples.en: The therapy aims to change the patient's mental representation of failure.
examples.cn: 这种治疗旨在改变患者对失败的心理表征。

examples.en: A map is public, but the route a driver follows is a mental representation.
examples.cn: 地图是公开的，而司机所循的路线是一种心理表征。

dict_mnemonic.text: 在心里给外部世界做一个小替身，替身不在场时也能拿出来看 → 心理表征

root: 拉丁 mens「心智」（词干 ment-）+ 拉丁 repraesentare「带到眼前」= 表示「再次」的前缀 + praesentare「呈现」（来自 praesens「在眼前」）；英语 mental representation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: something stands in for something else inside the mind, and that stand-in can be a picture, a concept, a memory, a meaning, a percept, a schema or the content of a belief.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个观念展开：某物在头脑内部替另一物站出来，而这个替身可以是画面、概念、记忆、意义、知觉、图式或信念的内容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded map carried in a pocket, standing for a city that is far away.
core.cn: 核心意象：口袋里一张折起的地图，替一座远方的城市站出来。

branches.en: THE STAND-IN: the base relation is replacement, not resemblance.
branches.cn: 替身：基础关系是替代，而不是相似。

branches.en: THE SENSES: what is seen or heard arrives already shaped as a picture.
branches.cn: 感官：所见所闻到达心智时已被塑成画面。

branches.en: THE FRAME: features and slots hold relations that a picture cannot.
branches.cn: 框架：特征与空位保存了图画无法保存的关系。

branches.en: THE TRACE: the stand-in outlives the event that produced it.
branches.cn: 痕迹：替身比产生它的事件活得更久。

branches.en: THE MEANING: words and beliefs point at content the mind must supply.
branches.cn: 意义：词语与信念指向心智必须提供的内容。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two Latin adjectives and nouns that also form large English families, one for the mind and one for standing in place of something.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个拉丁形容词与名词构成，它们各自形成庞大的英语词族，一个关于心智，一个关于代替某物。

latinIntro.en: Latin mens gives mental, mentality and mention-like words; repraesentare gives represent, representation and representative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mens 衍生 mental、mentality 等词；repraesentare 衍生 represent、representation 与 representative。

items.example: Mental effort can exhaust a person faster than physical work.
items.exampleCN: 脑力消耗有时比体力劳动更快让人疲惫。

items.example: The team's mentality changed after the first win.
items.exampleCN: 首场胜利之后，团队的心态变了。

items.example: The dots represent cities on the map.
items.exampleCN: 图上的点代表城市。

items.meaning: the act or result of standing for something
items.meaningCN: 代表或描绘的动作与结果
items.example: The painting is a representation of a harbour.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画是港口的表现。

items.example: The gallery shows representational art, not pure abstraction.
items.exampleCN: 这家画廊展出具象艺术，而非纯抽象。

items.meaning: serving as a typical example or delegate
items.meaningCN: 有代表性的；作为代表的
items.example: The sample is representative of the whole shipment.
items.exampleCN: 这份样本能代表整批货物。

items.meaning: to show or give; also being here now
items.example: She presented the findings to the board.
items.exampleCN: 她向董事会呈现了研究结果。

items.example: His presence quieted the room.
items.exampleCN: 他的在场让房间安静下来。

items.example: The advertisement misrepresents the size of the room.
items.exampleCN: 这则广告歪曲了房间的大小。

derivatives.meaning: the view that the mind works through representations
derivatives.meaningCN: 认为心智通过表征运作的主张

latinEntries.meaning: to bring before the eyes, represent

definition_zh: 象征性的；符号的；只有象征意义的；符号系统的；符号运算的
definition_en: standing for something else by association, or belonging to a system of signs
core_image: 一面旗子替一整支队伍站在广场中央，旗上没有一个士兵。
scene: 谈判桌上摆着一枚没有实际功能的木槌，双方都明白它代表的是最终决定权。The wooden gavel on the table is symbolic, standing for authority that no one can see.
sceneCN: 这里 symbolic 指「以联想方式代表另一事物的」（第 1 个义项：本身不是那件事物，却因共同承认而代表它）；句意为桌上那枚不能真正敲击的木槌代表看不见的最终决定权。可辨识物件：木槌、长桌、双方代表、空着的椅子。

pos.zh: 象征性的；符号的；仅具象征意义的

senses.title: Standing for something by association
senses.titleCN: 以联想关系代表另一事物
senses.definition: representing something else because a community or a person treats the sign as standing for it
senses.definitionCN: 因群体或个人把某一标记视为代表另一事物，从而具有代表作用
senses.example: The wooden gavel on the table is symbolic, standing for authority that no one can see.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上那枚木槌是象征性的，代表看不见的权威。
senses.why: The adjective names the relation, not the object: the sign is real, but what it points to is not present in it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词命名的是关系而非物体：标记本身真实存在，但它所指的东西并不在标记里面。

senses.title: Belonging to a system of signs
senses.definition: relating to signs that carry meaning by convention, as in symbolic language or symbolic notation
senses.definitionCN: 与按约定承载意义的符号有关，如符号语言或符号记法
senses.example: Chemists use symbolic notation to write reactions in one line.
senses.exampleCN: 化学家用符号记法把反应写成一行。
senses.why: A symbol works only inside a code, so the adjective also describes anything that belongs to such a code.
senses.whyCN: 符号只有在代码内部才起作用，因此这个形容词也描述属于这种代码的任何东西。

senses.title: In name only
senses.titleCN: 只是名义上的；仅有象征意义
senses.definition: having little practical effect and serving mainly to express a position or intention
senses.definitionCN: 几乎没有实际效果，主要用来表达立场或意图
senses.example: The fine was symbolic, but the ruling changed how firms behaved.
senses.exampleCN: 罚款只是象征性的，但裁决改变了企业的做法。
senses.why: When a gesture stands for an intention instead of producing an effect, it is called symbolic in a mildly critical way.
senses.whyCN: 当一个姿态只是代表某种意图、却不产生实际效果时，人们就带点批评地说它是象征性的。

senses.title: Relating to symbolism in art
senses.titleCN: 与艺术中的象征主义有关的
senses.definition: using visible forms to suggest inner states or ideas rather than to depict them directly
senses.definitionCN: 用可见形式暗示内心状态或观念，而不是直接描绘它们
senses.example: The symbolic imagery of the painting avoids any clear narrative.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画的象征意象避开了清晰的叙事。
senses.why: Symbolist artists made the sign carry the feeling, so the adjective became a period label as well as a description.
senses.whyCN: 象征派艺术家让标记承载感受，因此这个形容词既是一般描述，也成为一个时期标签。

senses.title: Manipulating signs rather than numbers
senses.definition: describing computation or logic that operates on formal expressions instead of numeric values
senses.definitionCN: 指对形式表达式而非数值进行操作的运算或逻辑
senses.example: Symbolic computation can solve the equation without approximating it.
senses.exampleCN: 符号运算可以直接解方程，而不必取近似值。
senses.why: Computer science distinguishes work on expressions from work on quantities, and calls the former symbolic.
senses.whyCN: 计算机科学把对表达式的处理与对数量的处理区分开，并把前者称为符号的。

senses.title: Carrying shared public meaning
senses.definition: expressing a value or identity that a group recognizes, such as a flag or a monument
senses.definitionCN: 表达某个群体所承认的价值或身份，如旗帜或纪念碑
senses.example: The bridge became symbolic of the city's recovery.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥成为这座城市复苏的象征。
senses.why: Public signs gather meaning from repeated use, so one object can stand for a whole shared history.
senses.whyCN: 公共标记在反复使用中积累意义，因此一个物件可以代表一整段共同历史。

senses.title: Ritual rather than literal
senses.titleCN: 仪式性的而非字面操作的
senses.definition: performed for its recognized meaning rather than for a practical result
senses.definitionCN: 因其被承认的意义而进行，而非为取得实际结果
senses.example: The first cut was symbolic, and the real work began afterwards.
senses.exampleCN: 第一刀是象征性的，真正的工作随后才开始。
senses.why: Ritual action is all meaning and little consequence, which is exactly the contrast the adjective draws.
senses.whyCN: 仪式性行动全是意义、少有后果，这正是这个形容词所划出的对比。

senses.title: Representing an abstract quantity
senses.definition: standing in for a variable or abstract entity in mathematics and formal systems
senses.definitionCN: 在数学与形式系统中代表变量或抽象对象
senses.example: In the proof, the letter is symbolic and can stand for any number.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个证明里，那个字母是符号性的，可以代表任何数。
senses.why: Algebra replaced particular numbers with letters, so a sign can now stand for a whole class of values.
senses.whyCN: 代数用字母取代了具体数字，因此一个标记现在可以代表一整类数值。

intro.en: Symbolic comes from Greek symbolikos, from symbolon, a token or sign, which passed through Latin symbolum and French symbolique into English.
intro.cn: symbolic 来自希腊 symbolikos，其词干 symbolon 指信物或标记，经拉丁 symbolum 与法语 symbolique 进入英语。

items.en: Symbolon named a token, often a half object matched with its other half to prove identity. It was built from a prefix meaning together and ballein, to throw, so the image is of things thrown together.
items.cn: symbolon 指信物，常为一件分成两半、以对合来证明身份的东西。它由表示「一起」的前缀与 ballein「投掷」构成，意象是把东西投到一起。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as symbolum, keeping the sense of a token, a creed or a sign by which something is recognized.
items.cn: 拉丁语借用该希腊词为 symbolum，保留「信物、信条、借以识别某物的标记」等义。

items.en: French formed the adjective symbolique, and English took it in the sixteenth century as symbolic, first in religious and then in general learned use.
items.cn: 法语造出形容词 symbolique，英语在十六世纪借入为 symbolic，先用于宗教，后进入一般学术用法。

items.en: Symbolism became the name of a literary and artistic movement, and symbolic gained the sense of suggesting inner states through visible forms.
items.cn: 象征主义成为一个文学与艺术运动的名称，symbolic 也获得「以可见形式暗示内心状态」的含义。

items.en: Logic and computing added the sense of working on formal expressions, giving phrases such as symbolic logic and symbolic computation.
items.cn: 逻辑学与计算机领域增添了「处理形式表达式」的含义，于是有符号逻辑、符号运算等说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of the throwing root): the pre-Greek history of ballein is not established, and any older form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（「投掷」词根的更深来源）：ballein 在希腊语之前的历史未获证明，凡为其提出的更早形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the sign family that look alike; group two holds adjectives for standing in place of something.
note.cn: 第一组是符号词族中形近的词；第二组是表示「代替某物」的形容词。

entries.definition: The mark or object that carries the meaning; symbolic is the adjective describing its relation to what it stands for.
entries.definitionCN: 承载意义的标记或物件；symbolic 是描述它与所指之物关系的形容词。

entries.definition: A system of symbols, or the artistic movement that uses them; it is a noun, not a description of one sign.
entries.definitionCN: 符号体系，或使用符号的艺术运动；它是名词，不是对单个标记的描述。

entries.definition: Indicating an underlying condition, from Greek piptein, to fall; the resemblance to symbolic is only in the shared prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 表明某种潜在状况，来自希腊语 piptein「落下」；与 symbolic 的相似只在共同前缀。

entries.definition: Balanced on two sides, from Greek metron, measure; it shares a prefix with symbolic but not a root.
entries.definitionCN: 两侧对称，来自希腊语 metron「尺度」；与 symbolic 共有前缀，却没有共同词根。

entries.definition: Serving as a visible emblem of a group or idea; it is close to symbolic but often suggests an official badge.
entries.definitionCN: 作为某个群体或观念的可见徽记；与 symbolic 相近，但常暗示正式的徽章。

entries.definition: Standing for a larger class because it is typical; symbolic standing comes from convention, not from being typical.
entries.definitionCN: 因具有典型性而代表更大的一类；象征性代表来自约定，而非典型性。

entries.definition: A small object or gesture that stands for something larger; token often stresses that the sign is minimal.
entries.definitionCN: 代表更大事物的小物件或姿态；token 常强调标记本身很小。

entries.definition: Existing as a name rather than a reality; this overlaps with the in-name-only sense of symbolic but lacks the sense of sign.
entries.definitionCN: 只作为名称而非现实存在；它与 symbolic 的「名义上」义重叠，但没有「符号」义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Greek token, the English sign family and the everyday gestures that mean more than they do.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：希腊信物、英语符号词族，以及那些意义大于实际作用的日常姿态。

normal.en: The Greek source is a token split in two, matched later to prove who is speaking.
normal.cn: 希腊语来源是一件分成两半的信物，日后对合以证明来者身份。

normal.en: The family runs symbol, symbolic, symbolically, symbolize, symbolism and symbolist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 symbol、symbolic、symbolically、symbolize、symbolism 与 symbolist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the two halves: symbolic meaning and symbolic computation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出两端：象征意义与符号运算。

normal.en: A flag is the clearest example: cloth and dye, yet a whole group stands behind it.
normal.cn: 旗帜是最清楚的例子：只是布与染料，背后却站着一整个群体。

normal.en: The phrase with of points at what is represented: symbolic of a new beginning.
normal.cn: 与表示「关于」的词连用，指出被代表之物：象征新的开始。

abstract.en: Picture a door key handed over in a ceremony but never used on a lock.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙在仪式上被交出，却从未插进任何锁。

abstract.en: Picture a wedding ring worn on a hand that works all day.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚婚戒戴在一只整天劳作的手上。

abstract.en: Picture a blank signature line that everyone treats as a promise.
abstract.cn: 想象一条空白的签名线，所有人都把它当成承诺。

examples.en: The handshake was symbolic, but it ended a decade of dispute.
examples.cn: 那次握手是象征性的，却终结了十年的争端。

examples.en: In symbolic logic, letters replace statements rather than numbers.
examples.cn: 在符号逻辑中，字母替代的是陈述，而不是数字。

examples.en: The colour red is symbolic of luck in many local festivals.
examples.cn: 在许多地方节庆中，红色象征好运。

dict_mnemonic.text: 一件小东西替一件大事站出来，所有人都认这个替身 → 象征的、符号的

root: 希腊 symbolon「信物、标记」= 表示「一起」的前缀 + ballein「投掷」，形容词 symbolikos；经拉丁 symbolum、法语 symbolique 入英语为 symbolic。ballein 更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one relation: a visible sign stands for something absent, and the same relation is then found in codes, empty gestures, art, computation, public memory, ritual and algebra.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种关系展开：一个可见标记替不在场之物站出来，这种关系随后出现在代码、空姿态、艺术、运算、公共记忆、仪式与代数中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flag on a pole holding the place of a whole crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：旗杆上的一面旗，占着一整群人的位置。

branches.en: THE RELATION: the sign is present where the meaning is not.
branches.cn: 关系：标记在场，意义却不在场。

branches.en: THE CODE: a sign means only because a system gives it a place.
branches.cn: 代码：标记之所以有意义，只因系统给了它位置。

branches.en: THE EMPTY GESTURE: meaning without consequence, done for what it declares.
branches.cn: 空姿态：有意义而无后果，为所宣告之事而做。

branches.en: THE ART: visible forms are asked to carry inner states.
branches.cn: 艺术：可见形式被要求承载内心状态。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC AND FORMAL: shared memory and formal manipulation both work through accepted signs.
branches.cn: 公共与形式：共同记忆与形式操作都通过被接受的标记运作。

intro.en: Symbolic is a Greek noun turned adjective, and its family covers signs, the study of signs and the act of making one thing stand for another.
intro.cn: symbolic 是由希腊名词转成的形容词，其词族涵盖符号、符号研究以及使一物代表另一物的动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin symbolum and Late Latin symbolicus carry the Greek term; English then adds noun, verb and adverb forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 symbolum 与晚期拉丁 symbolicus 承载这个希腊词；英语随后加上名词、动词与副词形式。

items.meaning: a sign that stands for something
items.example: The ring is a symbol of the promise.
items.exampleCN: 这枚戒指是承诺的象征。

items.example: The gift was symbolic rather than useful.
items.exampleCN: 这份礼物是象征性的，而非实用的。

items.example: The key was symbolically handed over.
items.exampleCN: 钥匙被象征性地交出。

items.example: White doves symbolize peace.
items.exampleCN: 白鸽象征和平。

items.meaning: a system of symbols or an artistic movement
items.example: The poem is dense with symbolism.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗象征意象密集。

items.example: The symbolist painted dreams, not scenes.
items.exampleCN: 这位象征派画家画的是梦，不是场景。

items.meaning: the act of representing by symbols
items.example: The symbolization of the river took centuries.
items.exampleCN: 这条河被符号化的过程历经数百年。

items.meaning: the study or use of symbols
items.example: The map's symbology is explained in the margin.
items.exampleCN: 地图符号的用法在页边有说明。

items.meaningCN: 缺乏象征意义或功能的
items.example: The test uses asymbolic shapes as controls.
items.exampleCN: 该测试用无象征意义的形状作为对照。

derivatives.meaning: in a way that stands for something else

definition_zh: 语言加工；语言处理；自然语言处理；文本处理
definition_en: the mental or computational handling of words and sentences, from sound to meaning
core_image: 一条流水线上，词句像零件一样被拆开、贴上标记、再装配成意义。
scene: 译者把一句话拆成词、标上词性，再按语法重新拼回去，屏幕上同时显示两层标记。The translator breaks a sentence into words and tags, a step of language processing that precedes the final draft.
sceneCN: 这里 language processing 指「对词句进行拆解与组合的加工过程」（第 1 个义项：心智或机器对语言材料进行的一系列操作）；句意为译者把句子拆词、标注再重组，这是定稿之前的语言加工步骤。可辨识物件：屏幕、词性标记、句子分块、译者。

pos.zh: 语言加工；语言处理；自然语言处理

senses.title: The mental handling of language
senses.definition: the set of mental operations by which a person turns sounds or marks into meaningful language
senses.definitionCN: 一个人把声音或书写标记转为有意义语言的一系列心理操作
senses.example: Language processing begins before a sentence is finished.
senses.exampleCN: 句子还没说完，语言加工就已经开始。
senses.why: The phrase names a series of operations, not a single act, because language must be handled in stages from input to meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语指一连串操作而非单一动作，因为语言必须从输入到意义分阶段处理。

senses.title: Understanding what is heard or read
senses.titleCN: 听懂或读懂时的理解加工
senses.definition: the operations that build meaning from incoming words, including access to word meaning and syntax
senses.definitionCN: 从不断到来的词中构建意义的操作，包括提取词义与句法分析
senses.example: Reading difficulties often trace back to slow language processing.
senses.exampleCN: 阅读困难常常可追溯到语言加工速度偏慢。
senses.why: Comprehension is the receiving half of the cycle, so it is treated as one branch of processing.
senses.whyCN: 理解是这一循环中接收的一半，因此被当作加工的一个分支。

senses.title: Putting language into words
senses.titleCN: 把意思组织成语言的产出加工
senses.definition: the operations by which a speaker selects words and builds a sentence to express an intention
senses.definitionCN: 说话者选择词语并构造句子以表达意图的操作
senses.example: The disorder affects language processing in speech but not in writing.
senses.exampleCN: 这种障碍影响口语产出的语言加工，却不影响书写。
senses.why: Production runs the same pipeline backwards, from intention to words, so it belongs under the same name.
senses.whyCN: 产出是把同一条流水线反向运行，从意图走向词语，因此也归在同一个名称之下。

senses.title: Machine processing of human language
senses.titleCN: 机器对人类语言的自然语言处理
senses.definition: the use of computer methods to analyse, tag or generate human language
senses.definitionCN: 用计算机方法分析、标注或生成人类语言
senses.example: Natural language processing lets a search engine answer a full question.
senses.exampleCN: 自然语言处理让搜索引擎能回答一个完整问题。
senses.why: The phrase was extended from minds to machines because both must break a string into units and assign them roles.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语从心智延伸到机器，因为两者都必须把字符串拆成单位并分配角色。

senses.title: Preparing text for analysis
senses.definition: the cleaning and marking of written material so that it can be searched, counted or classified
senses.definitionCN: 对书面材料进行清理与标注，使其可被检索、统计或分类
senses.example: The archive's language processing removed duplicate pages before indexing.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆的语言处理在建索引之前删除了重复页。
senses.why: Text needs preparation before any higher analysis, and the phrase covers that unglamorous middle stage.
senses.whyCN: 文本在进行更高层分析之前需要准备，这个短语正涵盖这段不起眼的中间环节。

senses.title: Handling speech as it arrives
senses.titleCN: 对实时到来的语音进行加工
senses.definition: the analysis of spoken input, including sound recognition and the mapping of sound to words
senses.definitionCN: 对口语输入的分析，包括声音识别与声音到词语的映射
senses.example: Spoken language processing must cope with accents and background noise.
senses.exampleCN: 口语语言处理必须应对口音与背景噪声。
senses.why: Speech adds a sound layer before words, so the same pipeline starts one stage earlier.
senses.whyCN: 口语在词语之前多了一层声音，因此同一条流水线要提早一个阶段开始。

senses.title: Applied systems such as translation
senses.definition: the use of language processing methods in products such as translators, summarizers and assistants
senses.definitionCN: 把语言处理方法用于翻译器、摘要工具与助手等产品
senses.example: Machine translation is the best-known application of language processing.
senses.exampleCN: 机器翻译是语言处理最广为人知的应用。
senses.why: When the pipeline is built into a product, the phrase shifts from the method to the service it performs.
senses.whyCN: 当这条流水线被装进产品，这个短语就从方法转向它所提供的服务。

senses.title: The research field itself
senses.titleCN: 作为研究领域的语言加工
senses.definition: the academic field that studies how humans and machines handle language
senses.definitionCN: 研究人与机器如何处理语言的学术领域
senses.example: She moved from psychology into language processing.
senses.exampleCN: 她从心理学转入了语言加工研究。
senses.why: A field is named by its object, so the activity becomes the name of the discipline that studies it.
senses.whyCN: 学科以研究对象命名，因此这一活动也成为研究它的学科名称。

intro.en: Language processing joins an Old French noun for speech to an English noun of action built on a Latin verb meaning to go forward.
intro.cn: language processing 把一个来自古法语、表示言语的名词，接在一个由拉丁动词「向前走」构成的英语动作名词上。

items.en: Lingua meant tongue and, by extension, language. Its deeper origin is generally considered to be a reconstructed form, and no single source is agreed.
items.cn: lingua 意为舌头，引申为语言。其更早来源一般认为是重构形式，学界并未就单一来源达成一致。

items.en: Old French langage named speech or a way of speaking, and English borrowed it as language in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 langage 指言语或说话方式，英语在十四世纪借入为 language。

items.en: Procedere meant to go forward, from pro, forward, and cedere, to go. Its noun processus named a course or progression.
items.cn: procedere 意为「向前走」，由表示「向前」的成分与 cedere「走」构成；其名词 processus 指进程或推进。

items.en: English process named a course of events or a method, and the ending -ing turned it into the name of an ongoing operation.
items.cn: 英语 process 指事件进程或方法，加上表示进行的名词后缀后，成为持续操作的名称。

items.en: Psycholinguistics and computing joined the two nouns in the twentieth century, one studying human handling of language and the other building machines to do it.
items.cn: 心理语言学与计算机领域在二十世纪把这两个名词组合起来，前者研究人如何处理语言，后者制造机器来做这件事。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin of tongue): the older source of lingua is a reconstructed form, and the exact date when the full phrase became standard is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（「舌头」义的拉丁语之前来源）：lingua 的更早来源属重构形式；整个短语成为标准说法的确切年代亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words from the two families that look alike; group two holds neighbouring fields and names for handling text.
note.cn: 第一组是两个词族中形近的词；第二组是相邻领域与处理文本的名称。

entries.definition: The system of words and rules itself; processing names what is done to it, not the system.
entries.definitionCN: 词语与规则的系统本身；processing 指对它做了什么，而非系统本身。

entries.definition: The academic study of language; language processing may be one of its objects, but the two are not the same field.
entries.definitionCN: 研究语言的学术学科；语言加工可以是它的研究对象之一，但两者并非同一领域。

entries.definition: A course of events, or to handle something by a method; processing is the ongoing form of that verb.
entries.definitionCN: 事件进程，或按方法处理某事；processing 是该动词的进行形式。

entries.definition: A set way of doing a task; it is a plan for handling, not the handling itself.
entries.definitionCN: 完成任务的固定方式；它是处理计划，不是处理本身。

entries.definition: The computing field devoted to machine handling of human language; it is the technical name for the machine sense.
entries.definitionCN: 专攻机器处理人类语言的计算领域；它是机器义的技术名称。

entries.definition: Handling written strings, often without any attempt to recover meaning; language processing usually goes further.
entries.definitionCN: 处理书面字符串，常不试图还原意义；语言加工通常走得更远。

entries.definition: Handling the sound signal itself, such as recognition or synthesis; language processing starts after or across that layer.
entries.definitionCN: 处理声音信号本身，如识别或合成；语言加工则在该层之后或跨越该层进行。

entries.definition: The understanding that results from processing; it is the outcome, while processing is the work.
entries.definitionCN: 加工之后产生的理解；它是结果，而加工是过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the tongue root, the going-forward root and the pipeline image.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「舌头」词根、「向前走」词根，以及流水线的画面。

normal.en: Language goes back to a Latin word for tongue; process goes back to a Latin verb for going forward.
normal.cn: language 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「舌头」的词；process 可追溯到表示「向前走」的拉丁动词。

normal.en: The pipeline has stages: sound, word, syntax, meaning, and sometimes output in another language.
normal.cn: 流水线有阶段：声音、词、句法、意义，有时还有另一种语言的输出。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the machine branch: natural language processing, spoken language processing.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出机器分支：自然语言处理、口语语言处理。

normal.en: The same word process appears in processor, procedure and procession, all from the going-forward root.
normal.cn: 同一个 process 还出现在 processor、procedure 与 procession 中，都来自「向前走」的词根。

normal.en: A translator's screen shows the stages at once: words, tags, syntax and the finished sentence.
normal.cn: 译者的屏幕同时显示各阶段：词、标记、句法与成句。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence entering a factory as raw parts and leaving as a finished machine.
abstract.cn: 想象一个句子以零件进入工厂，以成品机器离开。

abstract.en: Picture a river split into channels, each carrying one kind of meaning downstream.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河被分成多条水道，每条向下游运送一种意义。

abstract.en: Picture a loom that turns loose threads into one patterned cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一台织机把散线织成一整块有花纹的布。

examples.en: Children with language processing difficulties may hear words clearly yet struggle to follow a sentence.
examples.cn: 有语言加工困难的儿童可能把词听得很清楚，却难以跟上整个句子。

examples.en: The company uses language processing to sort customer reviews by complaint type.
examples.cn: 这家公司用语言处理按投诉类型给客户评价分类。

examples.en: Faster language processing does not always mean better understanding.
examples.cn: 语言加工更快并不总意味着理解更好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把语言当成原料送进流水线：拆词、贴标、拼句、出意义 → 语言加工

root: 拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」经古法语 langage 入英语为 language；拉丁 procedere「向前走」（pro- 向前 + cedere 走）的名词 processus 入英语为 process，加进行名词后缀成 processing。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pipeline: language arrives as sound or marks, is cut into units, assigned roles and rebuilt as meaning, and the same pipeline is run by minds, machines and research fields.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条流水线展开：语言以声音或标记到来，被切成单位、分配角色、重组为意义；同一条流水线由心智、机器与研究领域分别运行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a conveyor belt where loose words are tagged and assembled into a sentence.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条传送带上，散落的词被贴上标记并组装成句子。

branches.en: THE WHOLE CYCLE: the phrase names the entire run, not one station on the belt.
branches.cn: 整条循环：这个短语指整趟运行，而非传送带上的某一个工位。

branches.en: THE RECEIVING SIDE: sound and print enter and must be turned into units.
branches.cn: 接收端：声音与文字进入，必须先变成单位。

branches.en: THE SENDING SIDE: the same belt runs backwards from intention to sentence.
branches.cn: 发送端：同一条传送带从意图倒着运行到句子。

branches.en: THE MACHINE SHOP: computers perform the cutting and tagging at a different speed.
branches.cn: 机器车间：计算机以不同速度完成切分与标注。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT AND THE LAB: the pipeline becomes a service, and the service becomes a field.
branches.cn: 产品与实验室：流水线变成服务，服务又变成一个研究领域。

intro.en: The phrase is a compound of free English nouns, but each noun comes from a Latin family that also builds many related words.
intro.cn: 这个短语是两个自由的英语名词组成的复合，但每个名词都来自一个拉丁词族，各自还构成许多相关词。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua gives language, lingual and linguistics; Latin procedere gives process, procedure, processor and procession.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lingua 衍生 language、lingual 与 linguistics；拉丁 procedere 衍生 process、procedure、processor 与 procession。

definition_zh: 语言习得；母语习得；第二语言习得；语言学习过程
definition_en: the process by which a person comes to understand and use a language, especially without formal teaching
core_image: 一个孩子坐在餐桌旁，把大人们说的碎片一句句收进自己的小盒子，慢慢能拼成整句。
scene: 一个孩子在异国幼儿园待了一年，没有上过语法课，却能跟同伴讨价还价。After a year in a foreign kindergarten, the child's language acquisition outpaced every adult's textbook study.
sceneCN: 这里 language acquisition 指「在自然接触中逐步获得语言能力的过程」（第 1 个义项：不经正式教学而掌握语言的整体过程）；句意为孩子在异国幼儿园一年，语言习得的速度超过了成年人按课本学习。可辨识物件：幼儿园院子、同伴、孩子、玩具。

pos.zh: 语言习得；母语习得；第二语言习得

collocations.zh: 母语习得；第一语言习得

senses.title: Gaining a language as a whole
senses.titleCN: 整体获得一种语言能力
senses.definition: the process by which someone comes to understand and produce a language, whether at home or in a new community
senses.definitionCN: 某人逐步理解并产出一种语言的过程，无论在家庭还是在新社群中
senses.example: After a year in a foreign kindergarten, the child's language acquisition outpaced every adult's textbook study.
senses.exampleCN: 在异国幼儿园待了一年后，孩子的语言习得速度超过了成年人按课本学习。
senses.why: The phrase joins the whole system to the act of coming to have it, so it names a process rather than a lesson.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把整个语言系统与「逐渐拥有它」的动作连在一起，因此指一种过程，而非一堂课。

senses.title: Learning a first language at home
senses.titleCN: 在家庭环境中习得母语
senses.definition: the natural development of a first language in early childhood through everyday interaction
senses.definitionCN: 幼儿期通过日常互动自然发展出第一语言
senses.example: First language acquisition happens without a syllabus or a teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 母语习得没有教学大纲，也没有老师。
senses.why: The first language is acquired before schooling, so the general phrase is narrowed by the word first.
senses.whyCN: 第一语言在上学之前就已获得，因此「第一」一词把通用短语收窄到这一情形。

senses.title: Learning a later language in use
senses.titleCN: 在使用环境中习得第二语言
senses.definition: the development of a second or additional language through exposure and interaction rather than only through instruction
senses.definitionCN: 通过接触与互动、而非仅靠课堂教学发展出第二或更多语言
senses.example: Second language acquisition research asks why some learners stop improving.
senses.exampleCN: 第二语言习得研究追问为什么有些学习者会停止进步。
senses.why: The word second marks the later language, and acquisition marks learning by use rather than by rule memorization.
senses.whyCN: 「第二」标出较晚学习的语言，「习得」标出靠使用而非背规则来学习。

senses.title: Absorbing a language without lessons
senses.titleCN: 不经课堂而自然吸收语言
senses.definition: the uptake of a language from daily exposure, with little conscious study of grammar
senses.definitionCN: 从日常接触中吸收语言，几乎不有意识学习语法
senses.example: Her Spanish came from acquisition, not from evening classes.
senses.exampleCN: 她的西班牙语来自自然习得，而不是夜校课程。
senses.why: This sense draws the line between acquisition and learning that language teaching theory often insists on.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项划出「习得」与「学习」的界线，语言教学理论常强调这条线。

senses.title: A child's growing command of speech
senses.definition: the sequence of stages by which a child moves from first sounds to full sentences
senses.definitionCN: 儿童从最初的发音走向完整句子的阶段序列
senses.example: Child language acquisition moves from one word to many before grammar appears.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童语言习得先从一个词走向许多词，然后才出现语法。
senses.why: Researchers name the whole developmental sequence with the same phrase because each stage is part of one gaining.
senses.whyCN: 研究者用同一个短语命名整段发展序列，因为每个阶段都属于同一次获得。

senses.title: Growing up with two languages
senses.titleCN: 在双语环境中习得两种语言
senses.definition: the simultaneous or successive development of two languages in a young learner
senses.definitionCN: 年幼学习者在同一时期或先后发展出两种语言
senses.example: Bilingual acquisition can produce different strengths in each language.
senses.exampleCN: 双语习得可能在两种语言上形成不同的强项。
senses.why: The phrase is extended by the word bilingual, but the underlying process of gaining a system remains the same.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语被「双语的」一词扩展，但获得一个语言系统的底层过程并未改变。

senses.title: The research field that studies it
senses.titleCN: 研究语言习得的学科领域
senses.definition: the academic study of how languages are acquired by children and adults
senses.definitionCN: 研究儿童与成人如何习得语言的学术领域
senses.example: Language acquisition draws on psychology, linguistics and education.
senses.exampleCN: 语言习得研究借助心理学、语言学与教育学。
senses.why: As with other processes, the name of the activity becomes the name of the field that investigates it.
senses.whyCN: 与其他过程一样，活动的名称也成为研究该活动的学科名称。

senses.title: Gaining one specific part of a language
senses.titleCN: 习得语言的某一具体成分
senses.definition: the acquisition of a particular component such as vocabulary, a sound or a grammatical pattern
senses.definitionCN: 对词汇、某个语音或某种语法模式等具体成分的习得
senses.example: Vocabulary acquisition slows once a learner stops reading widely.
senses.exampleCN: 学习者一旦停止广泛阅读，词汇习得就会变慢。
senses.why: The whole process can be named for one of its parts, so the phrase also covers learning a single layer of language.
senses.whyCN: 整个流程可以用它的某一部分来命名，因此这个短语也涵盖学习语言的某一层。

intro.en: Language acquisition joins a noun carried from Old French to English with a Latin noun of action from acquirere, to get in addition.
intro.cn: language acquisition 把一个经古法语进入英语的名词，与来自拉丁 acquirere「额外取得」的动作名词连在一起。

items.en: Lingua meant tongue and language. Its deeper origin is generally considered to be a reconstructed form, and no single source is agreed.
items.cn: lingua 意为舌头与语言。其更早来源一般认为是重构形式，学界并未就单一来源达成一致。

items.en: Acquirere meant to get in addition, from a prefix meaning to or toward and quaerere, to seek. The image is of seeking something and adding it to what one already has.
items.cn: acquirere 意为「额外取得」，由表示「朝向」的前缀与 quaerere「寻找」构成；意象是寻得某物并把它加进已有的东西。

items.en: The action noun acquisitio passed through Old French acquisition into English, where it first named the obtaining of property or knowledge.
items.cn: 动作名词 acquisitio 经古法语 acquisition 进入英语，最初指获得财产或知识。

items.en: Language and acquisition were joined in learned writing, and the pair named the gaining of a language system rather than the gaining of a single word.
items.cn: language 与 acquisition 在学术写作中被组合起来，这一搭配指获得整个语言系统，而非获得单个词。

items.en: The phrase became a standard term in linguistics and psychology after the mid-twentieth century, when first and second language acquisition were studied as separate questions.
items.cn: 二十世纪中叶以后，这个短语成为语言学与心理学的标准术语，母语习得与第二语言习得被当作两个独立问题研究。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin of seek and the phrase's first fixed use): the older source of quaerere is a reconstruction, and no single first citation for the full phrase is established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（「寻找」义的拉丁语之前来源与该短语首次固定使用）：quaerere 的更早来源属重构；整个短语没有公认的最早书证。

note.en: Group one holds family members that differ in word class; group two holds names for neighbouring processes.
note.cn: 第一组是同族中词性不同的词；第二组是相邻过程的名称。

entries.definition: The act of obtaining something, from property to skills; language acquisition narrows it to one kind of obtaining.
entries.definitionCN: 获得某物的动作，从财产到技能；language acquisition 把它收窄到一种获得。

entries.definition: To obtain or come to have; the verb can take a language, a habit or a company as its object.
entries.definitionCN: 获得或逐渐拥有；这个动词可以带语言、习惯或公司作宾语。

entries.definition: Eager to possess things; it describes a person's attitude, not the process of learning a language.
entries.definitionCN: 渴望占有物品的；它描述人的态度，而非学习语言的过程。

entries.definition: Gaining knowledge or skill by study or experience; acquisition is often reserved for uptake without formal teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 通过学习或经验获得知识或技能；acquisition 常专指不经正式教学的吸收。

entries.definition: Gaining a language through lessons and deliberate practice; it contrasts with acquisition in teaching theory.
entries.definitionCN: 通过课程与刻意练习获得语言；在教学理论中与习得相对。

entries.definition: The growth of language ability over time, often used for children; it stresses change rather than the act of obtaining.
entries.definitionCN: 语言能力随时间成长，常用于儿童；强调变化而非获得动作。

entries.definition: The condition of using two languages; it is the result, while acquisition is the process that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 使用两种语言的状态；它是结果，而习得是产生它的过程。
