entries.definition: The ability to read and write; it is one outcome of language acquisition in a literate society.
entries.definitionCN: 读写能力；在有文字的社会中，它是语言习得的一项结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the tongue root, the seeking root and the child at the table.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「舌头」词根、「寻找」词根，以及餐桌旁的孩子。

normal.en: Language goes back to a Latin word for tongue; acquisition goes back to a verb meaning to seek and add.
normal.cn: language 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「舌头」的词；acquisition 可追溯到意为「寻找并增添」的动词。

normal.en: The contrast with learning is the key: acquisition happens by use, learning by study.
normal.cn: 与「学习」的对比是关键：习得靠使用，学习靠研读。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: first language acquisition, second language acquisition, child language acquisition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出分支：母语习得、第二语言习得、儿童语言习得。

normal.en: The same verb appears in acquire and acquisitive, one about gaining and one about wanting to gain.
normal.cn: 同一个动词还出现在 acquire 与 acquisitive 中，一个关于获得，一个关于想要获得。

normal.en: A child in a new playground learns the local words without a textbook, which is acquisition in the plainest form.
normal.cn: 孩子在新操场学会当地词语而不靠课本，这是最朴素的习得。

abstract.en: Picture a cup placed under a tap and filled drop by drop, with no one measuring.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子放在水龙头下，一滴一滴装满，没有人计量。

abstract.en: Picture a seed that needs only soil and time, not a written plan, to become a tree.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子只需要土壤与时间，不需要书面计划，就能长成树。

abstract.en: Picture a language entering a child through the ears and leaving through the mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象一种语言从耳朵进入孩子，又从嘴巴出来。

examples.en: Second language acquisition is faster when learners hear the language every day.
examples.cn: 学习者每天都能听到该语言时，第二语言习得更快。

examples.en: The study compared language acquisition in deaf children exposed to sign from birth.
examples.cn: 这项研究比较了从出生起接触手语的聋童的语言习得。

examples.en: Grammatical accuracy often arrives later than vocabulary in language acquisition.
examples.cn: 在语言习得中，语法准确往往比词汇来得更晚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 语言不是背来的，是像捡东西一样一点点「寻到并收进自己的袋子」→ 语言习得

root: 拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」经古法语 langage 入英语为 language；拉丁 acquirere「额外取得」= ad-（朝向）+ quaerere（寻找），动作名词 acquisitio 经古法语 acquisition 入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gaining: a person comes to have a language by use rather than by formal study, and the same phrase covers first, second, childhood, bilingual, partial and researched versions of that gaining.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次获得展开：一个人靠使用而非正式研读逐渐拥有一种语言；同一个短语涵盖母语、第二语言、儿童、双语、部分成分以及被研究的各种获得情形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child filling a small box with overheard phrases until whole sentences fit together.
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子把听来的短语收进一只小盒子，直到整句能拼在一起。

branches.en: THE WHOLE GAIN: language arrives by exposure, with no syllabus directing it.
branches.cn: 整体获得：语言靠接触到来，没有大纲指挥。

branches.en: THE FIRST HOME: the earliest language is gained before any classroom exists.
branches.cn: 第一个家：最早的语言在任何课堂出现之前就已获得。

branches.en: THE LATER LANGUAGE: a second system is added while the first stays in place.
branches.cn: 较晚的语言：第二个系统被加上去，第一个仍在原处。

branches.en: THE CHILD AND THE PAIR: development unfolds in stages, sometimes in two languages at once.
branches.cn: 儿童与成对：发展按阶段展开，有时两种语言同时进行。

branches.en: THE FIELD AND THE PART: the process becomes a discipline, and a single layer can be named alone.
branches.cn: 领域与部分：过程成为学科，单一层面也可单独命名。

intro.en: The phrase combines a noun from the tongue family with a noun from the seeking family; both have wide English families of their own.
intro.cn: 这个短语把「舌头」词族中的名词与「寻找」词族中的名词组合起来；两者各自都有庞大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua gives language, lingual and linguistics; Latin acquirere gives acquire, acquisition, acquisitive and acquirer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lingua 衍生 language、lingual 与 linguistics；拉丁 acquirere 衍生 acquire、acquisition、acquisitive 与 acquirer。

items.structure: Latin lingua through Old French langage
items.meaning: a system of speech or signs
items.example: Language is acquired before it is described.
items.exampleCN: 语言在被描述之前就已被习得。

items.meaning: to get or come to have
items.example: Children acquire sounds before words.
items.exampleCN: 儿童先获得语音，再获得词语。

items.meaning: the act or result of getting something
items.example: The acquisition of syntax takes years.
items.exampleCN: 句法的习得需要多年。

items.example: The acquisitive firm bought three rivals.
items.exampleCN: 这家热衷收购的公司买下了三家对手。

items.example: The acquirer kept the smaller firm's name.
items.exampleCN: 收购方保留了小公司的名称。

items.example: Acquired habits are hard to unlearn.
items.exampleCN: 已获得的习惯难以改掉。

items.example: Acquiring a language changes how one listens.
items.exampleCN: 习得一种语言会改变一个人倾听的方式。

items.example: Linguistic ability varies widely at age three.
items.exampleCN: 三岁时的语言能力差异很大。

items.example: Bilingual children switch codes with ease.
items.exampleCN: 双语儿童能轻松切换语言。

definition_zh: 获得；收购；习得；获得物；采集；取得
definition_en: the act or result of getting something, whether an object, a company, a skill or data
core_image: 一只手把新得的旧书放进自己的书架，另一只手把新钥匙放进抽屉。
scene: 公司董事会在长桌上签下一份文件，把另一家公司整个买进来，随后档案馆又开辟了新的一翼。The board approved the acquisition of a rival firm before the archive opened its own new wing.
sceneCN: 这里 acquisition 指「通过交易取得一家企业的所有权」（第 2 个义项：企业收购）；句意为董事会批准收购一家对手公司，随后档案馆才开辟新翼。可辨识物件：长桌、签字文件、公司徽标、档案馆新翼。

pos.zh: 获得；收购；习得；获得物；采集；取得

forms.label: 形容词（获取性的；贪得的）

senses.title: The act of getting something
senses.definition: the act of coming to have something that one did not have before
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐拥有此前没有的某物的动作
senses.example: The acquisition of a second desk solved the crowding.
senses.exampleCN: 添置第二张桌子解决了拥挤问题。
senses.why: The noun names the coming-to-have itself, whether the thing is bought, learned or received.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指「逐渐拥有」这件事本身，无论该物是买来的、学会的还是收到的。

senses.title: Buying control of a company
senses.titleCN: 收购一家企业的控制权
senses.definition: the purchase of a company or a controlling share of one by another company
senses.definitionCN: 一家公司购买另一家公司或其主要股份
senses.example: The board approved the acquisition of a rival firm before the archive opened its own new wing.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会批准收购一家对手公司，随后档案馆才开辟新翼。
senses.why: Business usage narrows the general act to one large purchase, where what is gained is control rather than an object.
senses.whyCN: 商业用法把一般性获得收窄到一次大型购买，所得到的是控制权而非物件。

senses.title: Coming to have a skill or language
senses.definition: the process of gaining a skill, a language or a habit through use or experience
senses.definitionCN: 通过使用或经验获得技能、语言或习惯的过程
senses.example: Acquisition of the local dialect took her two years.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了两年习得当地方言。
senses.why: Skills are gained gradually rather than bought, yet the same noun covers them because the result is still possession.
senses.whyCN: 技能是逐渐获得而非买来的，但同一个名词仍涵盖它，因为结果同样是拥有。

senses.title: Something newly gained
senses.definition: a thing or person newly obtained, often one that adds value to a collection or team
senses.definitionCN: 新近得到的物品或人员，常指为收藏或团队增添价值者
senses.example: The new goalkeeper proved a fine acquisition.
senses.exampleCN: 新守门员证明是一笔很好的引进。
senses.why: The act noun also names its product, so one can call the thing gained an acquisition.
senses.whyCN: 动作名词也指其产物，因此可以把得到的东西称为一项获得物。

senses.title: Adding materials to a library
senses.definition: the purchase or receipt of books and other materials for a library or archive
senses.definitionCN: 为图书馆或档案馆购买或接收书籍及其他资料
senses.example: The library's acquisition budget doubled last year.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆的采购预算去年翻了一倍。
senses.why: Libraries use the word for the routine adding of items, since each purchase enlarges the whole.
senses.whyCN: 图书馆用这个词指日常的添置，因为每次购买都在扩大整体。

senses.title: Collecting data or samples
senses.definition: the gathering of measurements, signals or specimens for later analysis
senses.definitionCN: 为日后分析而收集测量值、信号或标本
senses.example: Data acquisition ran all night while the sensor stayed fixed.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器固定不动，数据采集整夜运行。
senses.why: The word stresses the moment of capture, after which the material belongs to the researcher.
senses.whyCN: 这个词强调捕获的那一刻，此后材料就归研究者所有。

senses.title: Gaining a legal right or property
senses.titleCN: 取得法律上的权利或财产
senses.definition: the obtaining of ownership or a right through purchase, inheritance or another lawful means
senses.definitionCN: 通过购买、继承或其他合法方式取得所有权或某项权利
senses.example: The acquisition of the land required a public hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 取得这块土地需要举行公开听证。
senses.why: Law cares about when ownership passes, so the noun marks the precise moment of gaining title.
senses.whyCN: 法律关心所有权何时转移，因此这个名词标出取得产权的确切时点。

senses.title: Building a body of knowledge
senses.definition: the process of gathering facts or rules into a usable body of knowledge, as in expert systems
senses.definitionCN: 把事实或规则汇集为可用的知识体系，如专家系统中所做
senses.example: Knowledge acquisition was the slowest part of building the expert system.
senses.exampleCN: 知识获取是构建该专家系统最慢的一环。
senses.why: In information science the thing gained is knowledge itself, so the noun names its collection.
senses.whyCN: 在信息科学中，所得到的东西就是知识本身，因此这个名词指知识的汇集。

intro.en: Acquisition comes from Latin acquisitio, a noun of action from acquirere, to get in addition, built from a prefix meaning toward and quaerere, to seek.
intro.cn: acquisition 来自拉丁动作名词 acquisitio，其动词 acquirere 意为「额外取得」，由表示「朝向」的前缀与 quaerere「寻找」构成。

items.en: Quaerere meant to seek, ask or inquire. Its deeper origin is generally considered to be a reconstructed form rather than an established source.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻找、询问、探求。其更早来源一般认为是重构形式，而非已证实的来源。

items.en: A prefix meaning toward plus quaerere made acquirere, to get in addition. The picture is of seeking something and adding it to what one already holds.
items.cn: 表示「朝向」的前缀加 quaerere 构成 acquirere「额外取得」；意象是寻得某物并把它加进已有之物。

items.en: The action noun acquisitio named the getting, and its stem acquisit- is the source of the English form.
items.cn: 动作名词 acquisitio 指取得这一行为，其词干 acquisit- 是英语形式的来源。

items.en: Old French acquisition carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of obtaining property or knowledge.
items.cn: 古法语 acquisition 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语，最初指获得财产或知识。

items.en: Business, libraries, science and information technology each narrowed the word in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, giving the takeover, collection, sampling and knowledge senses.
items.cn: 商业、图书馆、科学和信息技术在十九与二十世纪各自收窄这个词，形成收购、入藏、采样与知识获取等义。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin of seek): the older source of quaerere is a reconstruction, and the exact date when the business sense became dominant is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（「寻找」义的拉丁语之前来源）：quaerere 的更早来源属重构；商业义成为主导的确切年代亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same seeking root with different prefixes; group two holds near names for getting something.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「寻找」词根、但前缀不同的词；第二组是表示「得到某物」的近义词。

entries.definition: Built with a prefix meaning back plus quaerere, it means to demand something as necessary, not to obtain it.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「向后」的前缀加 quaerere 构成，意为要求某物为必需，而非获得它。

entries.definition: A question or investigation, from the same seeking root; it names the search, not the thing gained.
entries.definitionCN: 提问或调查，同出「寻找」词根；它指寻找，而非所得到之物。

entries.definition: A query or doubt, from a closely related Latin noun; it is not the act of acquiring.
entries.definitionCN: 疑问或问题，来自一个关系密切的拉丁名词；它不是获得的行为。

entries.definition: Describing a person who is eager to acquire; it turns the act into a trait.
entries.definitionCN: 描述一个人渴望获取；它把行为变成一种性格。

entries.definition: Getting something by paying for it; acquisition is broader and can be free, legal or educational.
entries.definitionCN: 通过付钱得到某物；acquisition 更宽，可以无偿、法律性或学习性的。

entries.definition: The assuming of control over a company; it is one kind of acquisition, often hostile.
entries.definitionCN: 取得对一家公司的控制；它是收购的一种，常带敌意。

entries.definition: The organized purchasing of supplies, especially by an institution; it is a routine form of acquisition.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织地采购物资，尤指机构所为；它是获得的一种常规形式。

entries.definition: Gaining knowledge or skill; the acquisition of a skill is similar, but acquisition also covers objects and firms.
entries.definitionCN: 获得知识或技能；技能的获得与之相近，但 acquisition 也涵盖物品与公司。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the seeking root, the modern specialisms and the everyday act of adding something to a shelf.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「寻找」词根、现代各专门领域，以及把东西添到架子上的日常动作。

normal.en: The Latin verb means to seek and add: you look for something, then it becomes yours.
normal.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为「寻找并增添」：先找，随后它归你所有。

normal.en: The family runs acquire, acquisition, acquisitive, acquirer and acquired.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 acquire、acquisition、acquisitive、acquirer 与 acquired。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: mergers and acquisitions, data acquisition, library acquisition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：并购、数据采集、图书馆采购。

normal.en: The same root appears in require, inquiry and question, none of which mean getting a thing.
normal.cn: 同一词根还出现在 require、inquiry 与 question 中，它们都不表示得到某物。

normal.en: A library calls each new purchase an acquisition because it enlarges the whole collection.
normal.cn: 图书馆把每次新购称为一项入藏，因为它扩大了整个馆藏。

abstract.en: Picture an empty shelf receiving one book, then another, until it is full.
abstract.cn: 想象一个空架子先接到一本书，再接一本，直到装满。

abstract.en: Picture a key ring gaining a new key without losing any old one.
abstract.cn: 想象一串钥匙添了一把新钥匙，旧的并未丢失。

abstract.en: Picture a net that keeps widening as it catches more fish.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网捕到更多鱼时越张越宽。

examples.en: The museum announced the acquisition of a rare map.
examples.cn: 博物馆宣布入藏一幅珍稀地图。

examples.en: Language acquisition and language learning are often distinguished in teaching.
examples.cn: 在教学中，语言习得与语言学习常被区分开。

examples.en: The sensor's acquisition rate limits how fast the signal can change.
examples.cn: 传感器的采集速率限制了信号能变化得多快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 先「寻」到，再把它加进自己已有的东西里 → 获得、收购、习得

root: 拉丁 acquirere「额外取得」= ad-（朝向）+ quaerere（寻找），动作名词 acquisitio；经古法语 acquisition 入英语。quaerere 更早来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gain: something is sought and added to what one already has, whether the thing is a desk, a firm, a language, a book, a dataset, a title or a body of knowledge.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次获得展开：某物被寻得并加进已有之物，无论它是桌子、公司、语言、书、数据集、产权还是知识体系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open hand placing a newly found object on an already full shelf.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只张开的手把新找到的物件放到本已堆满的架子上。

branches.en: THE GENERAL ACT: seeking ends in having, whatever the object.
branches.cn: 一般动作：寻找以拥有告终，无论对象是什么。

branches.en: THE FORMAL TRANSFER: a company or a title changes hands by agreement or law.
branches.cn: 正式转移：公司或产权依协议或法律易手。

branches.en: THE INVISIBLE GAIN: a skill or a body of knowledge is built rather than handed over.
branches.cn: 看不见的获得：技能或知识体系是构建出来的，而非交接来的。

branches.en: THE THING AND THE SHELF: what is gained and the collection it joins share one name.
branches.cn: 物件与架子：所得之物与它所加入的收藏共用一个名称。

branches.en: THE CAPTURE: a signal is caught at a moment and becomes data.
branches.cn: 捕获：信号在某一刻被抓住，成为数据。

intro.en: Acquisition is a Latin noun of action whose verb is built from a prefix and a seeking root that also underlie several common English words.
intro.cn: acquisition 是拉丁动作名词，其动词由前缀与「寻找」词根构成，这两部分还构成若干常见英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin quaerere gives acquire, require, inquire and question; the prefix meaning toward narrows the family to getting something.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 quaerere 衍生 acquire、require、inquire 与 question；表示「朝向」的前缀把词族收窄到「取得某物」。

items.structure: ad- (Latin prefix, toward) assimilated before q
items.example: The prefix points the action at an object.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向某个对象。

items.example: The root carries the idea of searching.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带有「搜寻」的意思。

items.example: She acquired the habit in one summer.
items.exampleCN: 她在一个夏天里养成了这个习惯。

items.meaning: the act or result of getting
items.example: The acquisition closed in March.
items.exampleCN: 这笔收购在三月完成。

items.example: An acquisitive reader buys faster than she reads.
items.exampleCN: 一个贪多的读者买书快过读书。

items.example: The acquirer promised no layoffs.
items.exampleCN: 收购方承诺不裁员。

items.example: Acquired skills fade without use.
items.exampleCN: 已获得的技能不用就会衰退。

items.example: The job requires patience.
items.exampleCN: 这份工作需要耐心。

items.example: The inquiry lasted six months.
items.exampleCN: 调查持续了六个月。

definition_zh: 理解；理解力；阅读理解；听力理解；包含
definition_en: the ability or act of grasping the meaning of something, especially spoken or written language
core_image: 两只手掌把散开的页片合拢成一个完整形状，掌心之间露出全貌。
scene: 阅读课上，学生读完一篇短文后合上书，用自己的话说出作者的论证。Her comprehension of the passage showed when she restated the argument without notes.
sceneCN: 这里 comprehension 指「把握所读材料意义的过程」（第 1 个义项：把分散信息合拢为完整意义）；句意为她不用笔记复述论证，显示出对文章的理解。可辨识物件：合上的书、短文、学生、空白笔记本。

pos.zh: 理解；理解力；阅读理解；包含

forms.label: 复数（多种理解练习或理解事例）

senses.title: Grasping the meaning of something
senses.definition: the act of taking in the meaning of information and holding its parts together
senses.definitionCN: 接收信息的意义并把各部分合成一体的动作
senses.example: Her comprehension of the passage showed when she restated the argument without notes.
senses.exampleCN: 她不用笔记复述论证，显示出对文章的理解。
senses.why: The Latin verb behind the word means to grasp or seize, so comprehension is the mind taking hold of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁动词意为「抓取、握住」，因此理解就是心智把意义握住。

senses.title: The capacity to understand
senses.definition: a person's general ability to understand ideas or language
senses.definitionCN: 一个人理解观念或语言的一般能力
senses.example: The task was beyond the comprehension of the youngest students.
senses.exampleCN: 这项任务超出了最年幼学生的理解力。
senses.why: The same noun can name a lasting power rather than a single act, a common shift from action to capacity.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词可以指持久的能力而非单次动作，这是由动作转为能力的常见变化。

senses.title: Understanding a written text
senses.definition: the ability to read a text and recover its meaning, including implied relations
senses.definitionCN: 阅读文本并还原其意义、包括隐含关系的能力
senses.example: Reading comprehension improved once the class practiced summarizing.
senses.exampleCN: 班里开始练习概括之后，阅读理解提高了。
senses.why: Schools name the skill by its object, so reading plus this noun becomes a fixed label.
senses.whyCN: 学校用对象来命名技能，于是「阅读」加这个词成为固定标签。

senses.title: Understanding speech as it arrives
senses.definition: the ability to follow spoken language in real time and extract its message
senses.definitionCN: 实时跟上口语并提取其信息的能力
senses.example: Listening comprehension is harder when the speaker does not pause.
senses.exampleCN: 说话者不停顿时，听力理解会更难。
senses.why: Speech disappears as it is produced, so understanding it is named as a distinct skill.
senses.whyCN: 口语在产生的同时就消失，因此理解口语被命名为一项独立技能。

senses.title: The semantic side of language use
senses.titleCN: 语言使用中的语义理解
senses.definition: the construction of meaning from words and syntax during language processing
senses.definitionCN: 语言加工过程中由词语与句法构建意义
senses.example: Language comprehension can fail even when every word is known.
senses.exampleCN: 即使每个词都认识，语言理解仍可能失败。
senses.why: Knowing words is not enough; the mind must also assemble relations, which is what this sense names.
senses.whyCN: 认识词并不够；心智还必须组装关系，这一义项指的就是这件事。

senses.title: The sum of qualities in a concept
senses.definition: the set of attributes that a concept includes, as used in older logic
senses.definitionCN: 一个概念所包含的属性总和，为旧逻辑学所用
senses.example: In old logic, comprehension was opposed to extension.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧逻辑中，内涵与外延相对。
senses.why: This technical sense keeps the literal image of holding all the parts inside one boundary.
senses.whyCN: 这一专门义保留了字面意象：把所有部分都收在一个边界之内。

senses.title: Including something within a scope
senses.definition: the inclusion of something within a larger whole or category
senses.definitionCN: 把某物纳入一个更大的整体或类别
senses.example: The comprehension of small farms under one policy changed the map.
senses.exampleCN: 把小农场纳入同一政策改变了地图。
senses.why: The old inclusive sense survives in formal writing, where things are comprehended within a whole.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「包含」义保存在正式写作中，那里事物被收进一个整体。

senses.title: The limit of what can be understood
senses.definition: the range within which something can be understood, often used in the phrase beyond comprehension
senses.definitionCN: 某事物可被理解的限度，常用于「无法理解」这一说法
senses.example: The scale of the loss was beyond comprehension.
senses.exampleCN: 损失之大规模令人无法理解。
senses.why: A boundary is implied by grasping: what cannot be held inside the mind lies beyond comprehension.
senses.whyCN: 「握住」隐含边界：无法被心智握住的东西就落在理解之外。

intro.en: Comprehension comes from Latin comprehensio, a noun of action from comprehendere, to grasp or take together, built from com-, together, and prehendere, to grasp.
intro.cn: comprehension 来自拉丁动作名词 comprehensio，其动词 comprehendere 意为「抓住、合在一起」，由 com-「一起」与 prehendere「抓取」构成。

items.en: Prehendere meant to grasp or seize. Its deeper origin is generally considered to involve a reconstructed root, and the exact earlier form is not settled.
items.cn: prehendere 意为抓住、握取。其更早来源一般被认为涉及某个重构词根，确切更早形态尚无定论。

items.en: Com-, together, plus prehendere made comprehendere, to grasp together or take in. The physical image of closing a hand around something is original.
items.cn: com-「一起」加 prehendere 构成 comprehendere「合起来抓住、收进来」，原义是把手指合拢握物的具体意象。

items.en: The action noun comprehensio named the grasping, and also the inclusion of parts within a whole.
items.cn: 动作名词 comprehensio 指抓取，也指把各部分收进一个整体。

items.en: Old French comprehension brought the word into English in the fifteenth century, first in the sense of understanding and of including.
items.cn: 古法语 comprehension 在十五世纪把这个词带入英语，最初兼指理解与包含。

items.en: Reading and listening comprehension became standard labels in language teaching in the twentieth century, when tests separated reception from production.
items.cn: 二十世纪语言教学把阅读与听力理解变成标准标签，当时测试把接收与产出分开。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin of grasp): the older source of prehendere is a reconstructed form, and the exact moment when the educational labels became fixed is not recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（「抓取」义的拉丁语之前来源）：prehendere 的更早来源属重构形式；教育标签固定下来的确切时间没有记录。

note.en: Group one holds family words that differ sharply in meaning; group two holds near words for understanding.
note.cn: 第一组是同族中含义差别很大的词；第二组是表示「理解」的近义词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning complete or wide-ranging, as in a comprehensive report; it does not mean understanding.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为全面、范围广，如一份全面报告；它并不表示「理解」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning clear enough to be understood; comprehension is the act or power itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为清楚到可以被理解；comprehension 指理解的动作或能力本身。

entries.definition: From the same grasp root with a prefix meaning toward; it means understanding in older use, but now usually means fear of what may come.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「抓取」词根，前缀表示「朝向」；旧义为理解，现今通常指对将来之事的忧虑。

entries.definition: To consist of or include; it overlaps with the inclusive sense of comprehension but is a verb, not a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 由……组成或包括；它与 comprehension 的包含义重叠，但它是动词而非名词。

entries.definition: The general ability to grasp meaning or another person's position; comprehension is its more formal and often textual counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 把握意义或他人立场的一般能力；comprehension 是它更正式、常与文本相关的对应词。

entries.definition: A firm hold, physical or mental; to grasp an idea is the plain image that became comprehension.
entries.definitionCN: 牢固的握持，可为具体或心理的；把握一个观念正是变成「理解」的那个朴素意象。

entries.definition: The way something is seen or interpreted; it includes judgement, while comprehension stresses recovering meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 某物被看见或解释的方式；它包含判断，而 comprehension 强调还原意义。

entries.definition: An explanation of meaning that goes beyond recovering it, often adding a viewpoint.
entries.definitionCN: 对意义的解释，超出单纯还原，常加入某种视角。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the grasp root, the hand closing around parts, and the school labels for reading and listening.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「抓取」词根、把手合拢握住所握之物的画面，以及学校里的阅读与听力标签。

normal.en: The Latin verb means to grasp together: comprehension is the mind holding all the parts at once.
normal.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为「合起来抓」：理解就是心智同时握住所有部分。

normal.en: The family runs comprehend, comprehension, comprehensive, comprehensible and comprehensively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 comprehend、comprehension、comprehensive、comprehensible 与 comprehensively。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark school skills: reading comprehension and listening comprehension.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出学校技能：阅读理解与听力理解。

normal.en: The same root appears in apprehend, which shifts from grasping to fearing.
normal.cn: 同一词根还出现在 apprehend 中，其义从「抓住」转向「忧惧」。

normal.en: A closed hand around several loose pages is the whole word in one gesture.
normal.cn: 一只手合拢握住几张散页，就是这个词的全部动作。

abstract.en: Picture a net closing around many floating pieces at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网同时收拢许多漂浮的碎片。

abstract.en: Picture a reader's two hands bringing separate pages into one open book.
abstract.cn: 想象读者的双手把散页合成一本打开的书。

abstract.en: Picture a circle drawn around many dots so that they become one figure.
abstract.cn: 想象一个圈把许多点围进去，使它们成为一个图形。

examples.en: The manual is written for readers with no technical comprehension.
examples.cn: 这本手册写给没有技术理解力的读者。

examples.en: Her comprehension of the poem changed after she learned the history behind it.
examples.cn: 了解背后的历史之后，她对这首诗的理解变了。

examples.en: The speed of the lecture defeated the students' comprehension.
examples.cn: 讲座的速度使学生无法理解。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把散开的意义用手一把合拢握住 → 理解；把部分收进整体 → 包含

root: 拉丁 comprehendere「合起来抓住」= com-（一起）+ prehendere（抓取），动作名词 comprehensio；经古法语 comprehension 入英语。prehendere 更早来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one grasp: the mind closes around parts until they form a whole, and that gesture becomes a capacity, a school skill, a semantic act, a logical content, an inclusion and a limit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次抓取展开：心智把各部分合拢成一个整体，这个动作随后成为能力、学校技能、语义行为、逻辑内涵、包含与限度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands closing around loose pages until they form one book.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手把散页合拢，直到它们成为一本书。

branches.en: THE ACT: meaning is taken hold of, not merely received.
branches.cn: 动作：意义是被握住的，而非仅仅被接收。

branches.en: THE POWER: a single successful grasp becomes a lasting ability.
branches.cn: 能力：一次成功的抓取变成持久的能力。

branches.en: THE SKILLS: print and speech each demand their own timing.
branches.cn: 技能：书面与口头各自要求不同的时间节奏。

branches.en: THE MEANING: words must be assembled into relations before anything is understood.
branches.cn: 意义：词语必须先组装成关系，才谈得上理解。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY: what is included, what a concept contains, and what lies outside the grasp.
branches.cn: 边界：什么被纳入、概念包含什么，以及什么落在抓取之外。

intro.en: Comprehension is a Latin action noun whose verb joins a prefix of togetherness to a root of grasping; both parts build other English words.
intro.cn: comprehension 是拉丁动作名词，其动词把表示「一起」的前缀接在表示「抓取」的词根上；两部分都构成其他英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin prehendere gives comprehend, apprehend, prehensile and prison-like relatives; com- adds the sense of gathering into one.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 prehendere 衍生 comprehend、apprehend、prehensile 等词；com- 增添「收拢为一体」的意思。

items.example: The prefix gathers parts into one act.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把各部分收进同一个动作。

items.example: The root keeps the image of a closed hand.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根保留着合拢手掌的意象。

items.example: Few comprehend the scale of the change.
items.exampleCN: 很少有人理解这一变化的规模。

items.meaning: the act or power of understanding
items.example: Comprehension grew with each rereading.
items.exampleCN: 每重读一遍，理解就加深一层。

items.example: The report was comprehensive but hard to read.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告很全面，却难读。

items.example: The instructions are comprehensible to a beginner.
items.exampleCN: 这些说明初学者也能看懂。

items.example: The issue was comprehensively reviewed.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题得到全面审查。

items.example: He stared at the formula in incomprehension.
items.exampleCN: 他困惑地盯着那个公式。

items.meaning: to seize; to understand; to fear
items.example: The police apprehended the driver.
items.exampleCN: 警察抓住了司机。

definition_zh: 理解；领会；包含；抓住（古义）
definition_en: to grasp the meaning of something, or to include it within a whole
core_image: 手指把散落的小块拼成一整块，缺口终于对上。
scene: 一个孩子听完一段绕弯的故事后，忽然点头，把结局复述给旁边的同伴。The child paused, then began to comprehend the ending well enough to retell it.
sceneCN: 这里 comprehend 指「把握住某段内容的意义」（第 1 个义项：把分散信息合成可理解的整体）；句意为孩子停顿之后开始理解结局，并能复述出来。可辨识物件：孩子、同伴、故事书、点头动作。

senses.title: Grasp the meaning of something
senses.definition: to take in the meaning of information and hold its parts together as one
senses.definitionCN: 接收信息的意义，并把各部分作为整体握在一起
senses.example: The child paused, then began to comprehend the ending well enough to retell it.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子停顿了一下，随后开始理解结局，并能复述出来。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to grasp together, so the mental act is pictured as a hand closing around all the parts.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「合起来抓」，因此心理动作被描绘成一只手把各部分合拢握住。

senses.title: Follow what is said or written
senses.definition: to understand a particular sentence or utterance as it is heard or read
senses.definitionCN: 听懂或读懂某一个具体的句子或话语
senses.example: She comprehended the announcement before the translator finished.
senses.exampleCN: 译员还没说完，她就听懂了那则通告。
senses.why: This is the most common object of the verb: a specific string of words must be turned into a message.
senses.whyCN: 这是该动词最常见的宾语情形：一串具体的词必须被转成一条信息。

senses.title: Take in an abstract idea
senses.definition: to grasp an idea, principle or situation that has no single visible form
senses.definitionCN: 把握没有单一可见形态的观念、原则或处境
senses.example: Few new employees comprehend why the rule exists.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有新员工领会这条规则为何存在。
senses.why: An idea has no edges for the hand, so the grasp must be mental, yet the same verb serves.
senses.whyCN: 观念没有可供手抓的边缘，因此抓取只能是心理的，但同一个动词仍然适用。

senses.title: Include something within a whole
senses.definition: to contain or include something as a part of a larger whole
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为更大整体的一部分容纳或包括进来
senses.example: The old estate comprehends both the orchard and the mill.
senses.exampleCN: 这份旧地产既包括果园，也包括磨坊。
senses.why: The original physical sense of holding everything inside a boundary survives in formal legal and descriptive writing.
senses.whyCN: 把一切收在边界之内的原始具体义，保存在正式的法律与描述性写作中。

senses.title: Seize with the hand
senses.definition: to seize or grasp something physically, an older use now largely replaced by grasp
senses.definitionCN: 用手抓取或握住某物，这一旧义如今大多已被同义的抓握动词取代
senses.example: In the old tale, the hero comprehends the rope and climbs.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个古老故事里，主人公抓住绳子向上攀。
senses.why: This is the literal root meaning before it was borrowed for the mind; the modern word keeps the image but not the action.
senses.whyCN: 这是借给心智使用之前最字面的词根义；现代词保留意象，却不再指手的动作。

senses.title: Hold the whole picture
senses.definition: to understand how the parts of a complex matter fit together as a system
senses.definitionCN: 理解一件复杂事情的各部分如何作为系统组合起来
senses.example: Only the lead engineer comprehended the whole design.
senses.exampleCN: 只有主管工程师把握了整个设计的全貌。
senses.why: Understanding a system is grasping many relations at once, which is the strongest form of the original image.
senses.whyCN: 理解一个系统就是同时握住许多关系，这是原有意象最强的一种形式。

senses.title: Take in a difficult situation
senses.definition: to come to understand and accept the reality of a situation, often after resistance
senses.definitionCN: 在抗拒之后逐渐理解并接受某一处境的现实
senses.example: He could not comprehend the loss until he saw the empty room.
senses.exampleCN: 直到看见空房间，他才真正理解这次失去。
senses.why: Here understanding includes an emotional acceptance, because the fact must be held, not merely noted.
senses.whyCN: 这里的理解包含情感上的接受，因为事实必须被握住，而不只是被注意到。

senses.title: Cover something by a rule or class
senses.definition: to fall within the scope of a rule, category or definition
senses.definitionCN: 落在某条规则、某个类别或定义的范围之内
senses.example: The clause comprehends every case of accidental damage.
senses.exampleCN: 这一条款涵盖所有意外损坏的情形。
senses.why: The inclusive sense is used in law and logic, where a rule is said to hold a case inside its scope.
senses.whyCN: 包含义用于法律与逻辑，那里说一条规则把某个情形收在其范围之内。

intro.en: Comprehend comes from Latin comprehendere, to grasp together, built from com-, together, and prehendere, to grasp.
intro.cn: comprehend 来自拉丁 comprehendere「合起来抓住」，由 com-「一起」与 prehendere「抓取」构成。

items.en: Prehendere meant to grasp or seize. Its deeper origin is generally considered to involve a reconstructed root whose exact form is not settled.
items.cn: prehendere 意为抓住、握取。其更早来源一般被认为涉及某个重构词根，确切形态尚无定论。

items.en: Com- plus prehendere made comprehendere, to grasp together or take in. The physical sense came first and the mental sense grew from it.
items.cn: com- 加 prehendere 构成 comprehendere「合起来抓住、收进来」。具体义先出现，心理义由它生长出来。

items.en: Old French comprehendre carried the verb into English in the fourteenth century, already with the mental sense of understanding.
items.cn: 古法语 comprehendre 在十四世纪把这个动词带入英语，当时已带有「理解」的心理义。

items.en: The inclusive sense, meaning to contain within a boundary, remained in legal and descriptive writing long after the physical sense faded.
items.cn: 表示「收在边界之内」的包含义，在具体义消退很久之后仍留在法律与描述性写作中。

items.en: Comprehend and understand now divide the work: comprehensions are often formal or textual, while understanding is the everyday verb.
items.cn: 如今 comprehend 与 understand 分工：comprehend 常偏正式或偏文本，understand 则是日常动词。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin of grasp): the earlier source of prehendere is a reconstructed form, and the exact date when the mental sense became dominant is not firmly fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（「抓取」义的拉丁语之前来源）：prehendere 的更早来源属重构形式；心理义成为主导的确切年代亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds family members that differ in meaning or word class; group two holds other verbs for understanding.
note.cn: 第一组是同族中含义或词性不同的词；第二组是其他表示「理解」的动词。

entries.definition: The act or power of understanding; the verb is the act, the noun is the act or the capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 理解的动作或能力；动词指动作，名词指动作或能力。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning complete or wide in scope; it never means able to understand.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为完整、范围广；它从不表示「能理解」。

entries.definition: Built with a prefix meaning toward; it can mean to seize or to understand, and now often means to fear.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀表示「朝向」；它可指抓住或领会，现今常指忧虑。

entries.definition: To be made up of or include; it shares the inclusive sense but comes through a different French form.
entries.definitionCN: 由……构成或包括；它共有包含义，但经另一个法语形式而来。

entries.definition: The general verb for grasping meaning; comprehend is its formal counterpart and often sounds more bookish.
entries.definitionCN: 把握意义的通用动词；comprehend 是它正式的对应词，常显得更书面。

entries.definition: To hold firmly, literally or mentally; grasping an idea is the plain image behind comprehend.
entries.definitionCN: 牢牢握住，可为具体或心理的；把握一个观念正是 comprehend 背后的朴素意象。

entries.definition: To keep pace with what is said or happening; it stresses sequence, while comprehend stresses the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 跟得上所说或所发生之事；它强调顺序，而 comprehend 强调整体。

entries.definition: To understand the worth or significance of something, often with approval; comprehend can be cooler.
entries.definitionCN: 理解某物的价值或意义，常带赞许；comprehend 可以更冷静。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the grasp root, the formal register and the difference from understand.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「抓取」词根、正式语域，以及与 understand 的区别。

normal.en: The prefix means together and the root means grasp: to comprehend is to hold all the parts at once.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「一起」，词根意为「抓」：理解就是同时握住所有部分。

normal.en: The family runs comprehend, comprehension, comprehensible, comprehensive and comprehensively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 comprehend、comprehension、comprehensible、comprehensive 与 comprehensively。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark difficulty: hard to comprehend, fail to comprehend, comprehend fully.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出难度：难以理解、未能理解、完全理解。

normal.en: The same root appears in apprehend, which adds a prefix meaning toward and shifts from seizing to fearing.
normal.cn: 同一词根还出现在 apprehend 中，它加上表示「朝向」的前缀，并从「抓住」转向「忧虑」。

normal.en: Comprehend often takes a whole clause as its object, as in comprehend why the rule exists.
normal.cn: comprehend 常以整个从句作宾语，如「领会这条规则为何存在」。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing around several separate pieces until they click into one shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把几块分开的碎片合拢，直到它们咔哒一声拼成一个形状。

abstract.en: Picture a circle drawn around a scattered flock so that it becomes one herd.
abstract.cn: 想象一个圈把散开的羊群围住，使它们成为一群。

abstract.en: Picture a net lifted from the water with all its catch held inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网从水中提起，所有捕获都收在里面。

examples.en: The students could repeat the definition but not comprehend it.
examples.cn: 学生们能背出定义，却并不理解它。

examples.en: No one fully comprehends how the two systems interact.
examples.cn: 没有人完全理解这两个系统如何相互作用。

examples.en: The lease comprehends the garden as well as the house.
examples.cn: 这份租约既包括房屋，也包括花园。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把所有零散的部分合起来一把抓住，让它们成为一个整体 → 理解、包含

root: 拉丁 comprehendere「合起来抓住」= com-（一起）+ prehendere（抓取）；经古法语 comprehendre 入英语。prehendere 更早来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one grip: the hand closes around parts, and the same grip is then used for sentences, ideas, wholes, situations, legal scopes and the old physical act itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次握取展开：手把各部分合拢，这次握取随后被用于句子、观念、整体、处境、法律范围，以及古老的具体动作本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fingers bringing scattered pieces together until the gap closes.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指把散落的块拼在一起，直到缺口合上。

branches.en: THE GRIP: meaning is held rather than merely met.
branches.cn: 握取：意义是被握住的，而非仅仅被遇见。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a sentence and an idea are both held, one by the ear and one by the mind.
branches.cn: 对象：句子与观念都被握住，一个靠耳朵，一个靠心智。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY: a whole or a rule holds its parts inside a line.
branches.cn: 边界：整体或规则把各部分收在一条线内。

branches.en: THE OLD HAND: the literal grip survives in old stories and in the root itself.
branches.cn: 旧日的手：字面的握取留在古老故事与词根之中。

branches.en: THE WHOLE AND THE HARD CASE: a system, and then a loss, must be held before they are accepted.
branches.cn: 整体与难处：一个系统，随后是一次失去，都必须先被握住才谈得上接受。

intro.en: Comprehend is a Latin verb made of a prefix and a grasping root, and the same two pieces build a large English family.
intro.cn: comprehend 是由前缀与「抓取」词根构成的拉丁动词，同样这两部分构成一个庞大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin prehendere gives comprehend, apprehend, prehensile and the noun comprehension; com- adds the gathering sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 prehendere 衍生 comprehend、apprehend、prehensile 与名词 comprehension；com- 增添「收拢」义。

items.example: The prefix makes the grasping collective.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使抓取成为收拢一体的动作。

items.example: The root supplies the physical image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供具体意象。

items.example: She comprehends the rule now.
items.exampleCN: 她现在理解这条规则了。

items.example: Comprehension takes time.
items.exampleCN: 理解需要时间。

items.example: The note is comprehensible at a glance.
items.exampleCN: 这张便条一眼就能看懂。

items.example: A comprehensive list fills two pages.
items.exampleCN: 一份全面清单写满两页。

items.example: The comprehending reader notices the tone.
items.exampleCN: 有理解力的读者会注意到语气。

items.meaning: to seize; to understand; to fear
items.example: They apprehended the meaning slowly.
items.exampleCN: 他们慢慢领会了那层意思。

items.example: The animal has a prehensile tail.
items.exampleCN: 这种动物有一条能抓握的尾巴。

definition_zh: 可视化；视觉化想象；数据可视化；图示结果
definition_en: the act or result of making something visible or of forming a picture of it in the mind
core_image: 一团看不出形状的数字被折成一条起伏的曲线，曲线自己讲出高低。
scene: 会议室里，原本密密麻麻的表格被换成一张曲线图，大家一眼看出哪个月最忙。The meeting shifted from a dense table to a line chart, a visualization that made the busy month obvious.
sceneCN: 这里 visualization 指「把信息转成看得见的图形」（第 1 个义项：让抽象信息以视觉形式呈现）；句意为会议从密集表格改用折线图，这一可视化使最忙的月份一目了然。可辨识物件：投影屏幕、折线图、密集表格、会议室。

pos.zh: 可视化；视觉化；图示结果

forms.label: 复数（多种图示或视觉化实例）

derivatives.zh: 可视化工具；擅长视觉想象的人

senses.title: Making information visible
senses.definition: the act of turning abstract information into a visual form that can be seen and read quickly
senses.definitionCN: 把抽象信息转成可被快速看见与读取的视觉形式的动作
senses.example: The meeting shifted from a dense table to a line chart, a visualization that made the busy month obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 会议从密集表格改用折线图，这一可视化让最忙的月份一目了然。
senses.why: The noun names the making-visible itself, so anything that turns numbers into shapes belongs here.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指「使可见」这件事本身，因此凡把数字变成形状的做法都属于这一义项。

senses.title: Forming a picture in the mind
senses.definition: the mental act of picturing an object, place or outcome that is not present
senses.definitionCN: 在对象、地点或结果不在场时于脑中形成画面的心理动作
senses.example: Visualization before a race can steady a runner's breathing.
senses.exampleCN: 赛前的视觉化想象能让跑者的呼吸稳定下来。
senses.why: The same word is used for the mind's eye, because the inner picture is also something made visible to oneself.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也用于心灵之眼，因为内心画面同样是让自己看见的东西。

senses.title: Charts for exploring data
senses.definition: the field and practice of representing datasets with charts, maps or interactive graphics
senses.definitionCN: 用图表、地图或交互图形表现数据集的领域与实践
senses.example: Good data visualization shows the outlier without hiding the spread.
senses.exampleCN: 好的数据可视化既显示离群值，又不掩盖分布范围。
senses.why: Data work adopted the word because a chart lets a person see patterns that a table only stores.
senses.whyCN: 数据工作采用这个词，因为图表让人看见表格只是储存着的模式。

senses.title: Rendering scientific models
senses.titleCN: 科学模型的可视化呈现
senses.definition: the use of computer graphics to show simulations, fields or structures that cannot be directly seen
senses.definitionCN: 用计算机图形显示无法直接看见的模拟、场或结构
senses.example: Scientific visualization turned the airflow into a moving surface.
senses.exampleCN: 科学可视化把气流变成一张移动的曲面。
senses.why: Science often computes what no eye can watch, so graphics become the only way to inspect it.
senses.whyCN: 科学常常计算眼睛看不到的东西，因此图形成为查看它的唯一方式。

senses.title: Showing the inside of the body
senses.definition: the production of images of internal anatomy for diagnosis or teaching
senses.definitionCN: 为诊断或教学生成身体内部解剖图像
senses.example: The software's visualization of the artery guided the surgeon.
senses.exampleCN: 该软件对动脉的可视化呈现为外科医生提供了指引。
senses.why: Medical imaging makes tissue visible without opening the body, which is the word's promise in its most literal form.
senses.whyCN: 医学影像不打开身体就让组织可见，这是这个词最字面的兑现。

senses.title: A visual presentation
senses.definition: a diagram, model or display used to communicate an idea to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 用于向受众传达观念的图示、模型或展示
senses.example: Her visualization of the timeline used colour instead of words.
senses.exampleCN: 她对时间线的视觉化呈现用颜色代替文字。
senses.why: The word can name the display itself, not only the act of making it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以指展示物本身，而不只是制作它的动作。

senses.title: The image produced
senses.definition: the output image or graphic that results from a visualization process
senses.definitionCN: 可视化过程所产生的输出图像或图形
senses.example: The final visualization revealed a gap no one had expected.
senses.exampleCN: 最终图像揭示出一个谁都没预料到的缺口。
senses.why: As an action noun, the word also names its product, so the chart on the wall is a visualization.
senses.whyCN: 作为动作名词，这个词也指其产物，因此墙上的图表本身就是一件可视化作品。

senses.title: The methods and tools involved
senses.definition: the set of techniques and software used to produce visual representations
senses.definitionCN: 用于产出视觉表征的技术与软件集合
senses.example: The lab invested in visualization rather than in more sensors.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室把钱投在可视化技术上，而不是添置更多传感器。
senses.why: A practice grows into a toolkit, and the name of the practice comes to name the toolkit.
senses.whyCN: 实践会成长为一套工具，实践的名称也就成了工具的名称。

intro.en: Visualization is an English noun built on visual, from Late Latin visualis, of sight, plus the action suffix -ization.
intro.cn: visualization 是英语名词，建立在 visual 之上；visual 来自晚期拉丁 visualis「视觉的」，再加动作名词后缀。

items.en: Videre meant to see. Its deeper origin is generally considered to be a reconstructed Indo-European root, and the exact earlier shape is not settled.
items.cn: videre 意为看见。其更早来源一般认为是某个印欧语词根，确切更早形态尚无定论。

items.en: Visus meant sight or the act of seeing, and also served as the past participle of videre; both noun and participle feed the English family.
items.cn: visus 意为视觉或看见这一动作，同时兼作 videre 的过去分词；名词与分词两条线都进入英语词族。

items.en: Visualis meant relating to sight, and English visual entered in the fifteenth century through French.
items.cn: visualis 意为与视觉有关的；英语 visual 在十五世纪经法语进入。

items.en: The action suffix -ization turned adjectives into nouns of process, giving visualization as the making of something visible.
items.cn: 表示动作的名词后缀把形容词变成过程名词，于是 visualization 指「使某物可见」的过程。

items.en: Data and scientific visualization became named fields in the late twentieth century, when graphics hardware made large datasets viewable.
items.cn: 数据可视化与科学可视化在二十世纪后期成为有名称的领域，当时图形硬件使大型数据集可被观看。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date of the noun and pre-Latin origin of see): the earliest English record of visualization is not firmly dated, and the deeper source of videre is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（该名词首见年代与「看见」义的拉丁语之前来源）：visualization 最早的英语记录没有确切年代；videre 的更早来源属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the sight family that differ in function; group two holds names for visual displays.
note.cn: 第一组是视觉词族中功能不同的词；第二组是视觉展示物的名称。

entries.definition: Relating to sight or to something seen; visualization is the act or product of making something visual.
entries.definitionCN: 与视觉或所见之物有关的；visualization 是使某物视觉化的动作或产物。

entries.definition: To make visible or to form a mental picture; the noun names the act or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 使可见或在脑中形成画面；名词指该动作或其结果。

entries.definition: The power of seeing, or a grand plan for the future; it is not the act of turning data into a chart.
entries.definitionCN: 视力，或对未来的宏大设想；它不是把数据变成图表的动作。

entries.definition: Able to be seen; visualization can produce something visible, but the adjective says nothing about the process.
entries.definitionCN: 能被看见的；可视化可以产生可见之物，但这个形容词不涉及过程。

entries.definition: A graphic display of data, often one kind of visualization; the chart is the object, visualization also names the method.
entries.definitionCN: 数据的图形展示，常是可视化的一种；图表是物件，visualization 也指方法。

entries.definition: A simplified drawing that explains how something works; it need not involve data.
entries.definitionCN: 解释某物如何运作的简化图；不一定涉及数据。

entries.definition: Pictures or descriptive language that create pictures in the mind; visualization is the act of making such pictures.
entries.definitionCN: 在脑中造出画面的图像或描写性语言；visualization 是制造这类画面的动作。

entries.definition: An image produced by computer graphics from a model; it is one technical kind of visualization output.
entries.definitionCN: 由计算机图形从模型生成的图像；它是可视化输出的一种技术类型。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the see root, the making-visible suffix and the chart that replaces a table.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「看见」词根、表示「使成为」的后缀，以及取代表格的图表。

normal.en: Visual comes from a Latin word for sight; the suffix turns the adjective into the act of making something visible.
normal.cn: visual 来自拉丁语中表示「视觉」的词；后缀把这个形容词变成「使某物可见」的动作。

normal.en: The family runs visual, visualize, visualization, visually, vision and visible.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 visual、visualize、visualization、visually、vision 与 visible。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: data visualization, scientific visualization, visualization tool.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：数据可视化、科学可视化、可视化工具。

normal.en: The word covers both the act and the object: a visualization is both the making and the chart itself.
normal.cn: 这个词兼指动作与物件：一件可视化作品既是制作过程，也是图表本身。

normal.en: The mind's eye does the same thing without a screen: athletes visualize a race before running it.
normal.cn: 心灵之眼不用屏幕也能做同样的事：运动员在起跑前先在脑中过一遍赛程。

abstract.en: Picture numbers folding themselves into a mountain range on a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象数字在屏幕上把自己折成一道山脉。

abstract.en: Picture a blindfolded runner seeing the whole track before the start.
abstract.cn: 想象一个蒙住眼睛的跑者在起跑前看见整条跑道。

abstract.en: Picture a map that draws itself from a million addresses.
abstract.cn: 想象一张由百万个地址自己画出来的地图。

examples.en: The report's visualization made the seasonal pattern visible at a glance.
examples.cn: 报告的可视化让季节性规律一眼可见。

examples.en: Surgeons rehearsed the operation through a three-dimensional visualization.
examples.cn: 外科医生通过三维可视化预演了这台手术。

examples.en: Visualization alone does not prove a hypothesis; it only helps one see it.
examples.cn: 可视化本身不能证明假设，只能帮助人看见它。

dict_mnemonic.text: 让看不见的东西长出眼睛能认出的形状 → 可视化

root: 拉丁 videre「看见」→ 过去分词 visus「视觉」→ 晚期拉丁 visualis「视觉的」→ 英语 visual；加动作名词后缀成 visualization。videre 更早来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one making-visible: data, models, anatomy, ideas and inner pictures are all given a shape the eye can take in, and the word names the act, the object and the toolkit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次「使可见」展开：数据、模型、解剖结构、观念与内心画面都被赋予眼睛能接收的形状；这个词兼指动作、物件与工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shapeless column of numbers folded into a readable curve.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团没有形状的数字被折成一条可读的曲线。

branches.en: THE ACT: the base sense is simply making something visible.
branches.cn: 动作：基础义就是把某物变得可见。

branches.en: THE INNER EYE: the same act happens without a screen.
branches.cn: 内心之眼：同样的动作也能在没有屏幕时发生。

branches.en: THE DATASET AND THE MODEL: numbers and simulations acquire surfaces.
branches.cn: 数据集与模型：数字与模拟获得表面。

branches.en: THE BODY: tissue becomes visible without being opened.
branches.cn: 身体：组织不必被打开就能被看见。

branches.en: THE DISPLAY, THE IMAGE AND THE TOOL: communication, output and method each take the name.
branches.cn: 展示、图像与工具：传达、输出与方法各自取用这个名称。

intro.en: Visualization is built from a Latin adjective of sight and an English noun suffix that names a process.
intro.cn: visualization 由拉丁语中表示视觉的形容词与一个表示过程的英语名词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and its participle visus give vision, visible, visual and visualize; the suffix then builds visualization.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 videre 及其分词 visus 衍生 vision、visible、visual 与 visualize；后缀随后构成 visualization。

items.example: The root underlies every word in this family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根支撑着这一词族的每个词。

items.example: The visual evidence was stronger than the testimony.
items.exampleCN: 视觉证据比证词更有力。

items.example: The two pages are visually identical.
items.exampleCN: 这两页在视觉上完全相同。

items.example: Her vision for the square won the competition.
items.exampleCN: 她对广场的设想赢得了竞赛。

items.example: The scar is barely visible.
items.exampleCN: 那道疤几乎看不见。

items.example: Fog cut visibility to a few metres.
items.exampleCN: 雾把能见度降到几米。

items.meaning: to make visible or picture mentally
items.example: The program visualizes the traffic flow.
items.exampleCN: 这个程序把交通流可视化。

items.meaning: the act or result of making visible
items.example: The visualization filled the whole wall.
items.exampleCN: 这幅可视化图占满了整面墙。

items.meaning: a tool or person that visualizes
items.meaningCN: 可视化工具；擅长视觉想象的人
items.example: The visualizer plots each sensor in real time.
items.exampleCN: 这个可视化工具实时绘制每个传感器。

derivatives.meaning: a person who works with visual means
a person or tool that makes something visible
derivatives.meaningCN: 把数据或想法变成图像的人或工具

definition_zh: 在脑中想象；使可视化；预想；用图形表示
definition_en: to form a picture of something in the mind, or to make data visible in a graphic form
core_image: 一个设计师在空白纸面上先看见成品的样子，再落笔。
scene: 跑步运动员在起跑前闭上眼，把整段赛程在脑中过了一遍，连转弯的角度都清楚。Before the race, runners visualize the turns and the finish line.
sceneCN: 这里 visualize 指「在脑中把不在眼前的事物形成画面」（第 1 个义项：用心灵之眼构建视觉形象）；句意为跑者在起跑前闭上眼，在脑中过一遍弯道与终点。可辨识物件：起跑线、闭眼的跑者、弯道标记、终点线。

pos.zh: 在脑中想象；使可视化；预想

derivatives.zh: 可视化工具；擅长视觉想象的人
已可视化的；被想象出来的

senses.title: Form a picture in the mind
senses.definition: to create a visual image of something that is not physically present
senses.definitionCN: 为不在眼前的事物在脑中造出视觉形象
senses.example: Before the race, runners visualize the turns and the finish line.
senses.exampleCN: 起跑之前，跑者会在脑中想象弯道与终点线。
senses.why: The verb is visual plus a suffix meaning to make, so it means to make something visible to oneself.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词由「视觉的」加表示「使成为」的后缀构成，因此意为「使自己看见某物」。

senses.title: Picture a future outcome
senses.definition: to imagine a result before it happens, often in order to prepare for it
senses.definitionCN: 在结果发生之前想象它，常为做准备
senses.example: She visualized the interview going badly and planned her answers.
senses.exampleCN: 她预想面试可能不顺利，并据此准备了回答。
senses.why: A future event has no picture yet, so the mind must supply one deliberately.
senses.whyCN: 未来事件尚无画面，因此心智必须有意识地提供一幅。

senses.title: Turn data into a chart
senses.definition: to represent numerical data with a graphic that can be read at a glance
senses.definitionCN: 用一眼可读的图形来表现数值数据
senses.example: The tool visualizes the annual rainfall as a heat map.
senses.exampleCN: 这个工具把年降雨量显示为热力图。
senses.why: Computing shortened the phrase make visible to the single verb, and data is now its most common object.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域把「使可见」压缩成一个动词，而数据如今是它最常见的宾语。

senses.title: Give abstract information a shape
senses.definition: to depict relations, processes or quantities in a diagrammatic form
senses.definitionCN: 以图示形式描绘关系、过程或数量
senses.example: The lecture visualized the feedback loop as a circle of arrows.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座把反馈回路画成一圈箭头。
senses.why: Anything abstract can be given edges on a page, which is what the verb asks the mind or the software to do.
senses.whyCN: 任何抽象事物都能在纸面上获得边缘，这正是这个动词要求心智或软件去做的事。

senses.title: Display internal anatomy
senses.definition: to produce an image of structures inside the body for diagnosis or teaching
senses.definitionCN: 为诊断或教学生成身体内部结构的图像
senses.example: The scan visualizes the tear in the ligament.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描把韧带上的撕裂显示出来。
senses.why: Medical imaging makes hidden tissue visible, so the verb's literal promise is fulfilled.
senses.whyCN: 医学影像让隐藏的组织变得可见，这个动词的字面承诺由此兑现。

senses.title: See something clearly
senses.definition: to see something distinctly with the eyes, a sense now rare outside technical writing
senses.definitionCN: 用眼睛清楚地看见某物，这一义项如今多见于技术写作
senses.example: The stain was visualized only under ultraviolet light.
senses.exampleCN: 那处污渍只有在紫外光下才显现出来。
senses.why: Before the mental sense dominated, the verb meant to make or see a thing visibly, and traces remain in laboratory use.
senses.whyCN: 在心理义占主导之前，这个动词指使某物可见或用眼看见，实验室用法中仍留有其痕迹。

senses.title: Imagine a design before building it
senses.definition: to picture how a structure, page or product will look and work before it exists
senses.definitionCN: 在结构、页面或产品存在之前想象它的样子与运作
senses.example: The architect visualized the staircase before drawing a line.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师在画下第一根线之前已经想见那段楼梯。
senses.why: Design work depends on seeing an absent object early, so visualization becomes a planning act.
senses.whyCN: 设计工作依赖提早看见尚不存在的对象，于是视觉化想象成为一种规划行为。

senses.title: Explain by showing a picture
senses.definition: to present an idea to others through a drawing, diagram or animation
senses.definitionCN: 通过图画、图示或动画向他人呈现一个观念
senses.example: He visualized the process for the class with three boxes and an arrow.
senses.exampleCN: 他用三个方框和一个箭头向全班图示了这个过程。
senses.why: The verb can point outward as well as inward: the picture is made for another person's eyes.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词既可向内也可向外：画面是为别人的眼睛而造的。

intro.en: Visualize is an English verb formed from visual plus the suffix -ize, which means to make or to render.
intro.cn: visualize 是由 visual 加表示「使成为、使呈现」的后缀构成的英语动词。

items.en: Videre meant to see. Its deeper origin is generally considered to be a reconstructed Indo-European root, and the exact earlier shape is not settled.
items.cn: videre 意为看见。其更早来源一般认为是某个印欧语词根，确切更早形态尚无定论。

items.en: Visus meant sight and also served as the past participle of videre, so the same stem feeds nouns and adjectives alike.
items.cn: visus 意为视觉，同时兼作 videre 的过去分词，因此同一词干同时供给名词与形容词。

items.en: Visualis meant relating to sight; English visual arrived through French in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: visualis 意为与视觉有关的；英语 visual 在十五世纪经法语进入。

items.en: Visual plus -ize produced visualize in the nineteenth century, first in the sense of making something visible to the eye.
items.cn: visual 加动词后缀在十九世纪造出 visualize，最初指使某物对眼睛可见。

items.en: The mental sense of picturing something grew in psychology, and the data sense grew with computer graphics in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 在脑中形成画面的心理义在心理学中发展，数据义则随二十世纪的计算机图形学成长。

items.en: Source uncertain (exact first date and pre-Latin origin of see): the earliest citation for the verb is not firmly fixed, and the deeper source of videre is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（确切首见年代与「看见」义的拉丁语之前来源）：该动词最早的书面记录没有定论；videre 的更早来源属重构。

note.en: Group one holds sight-family words that differ in function; group two holds verbs for imagining.
note.cn: 第一组是视觉词族中功能不同的词；第二组是表示「想象」的动词。

entries.definition: Relating to sight; the verb adds the act of making or picturing, while the adjective only describes.
entries.definitionCN: 与视觉有关的；动词加上「使成为或想象」的动作，而形容词只作描述。

entries.definition: The act or result of visualizing; the verb is what a person or program does.
entries.definitionCN: 视觉化的动作或结果；动词指人或程序所做的事。

entries.definition: The power of seeing or a large future plan; it is not the deliberate act of picturing a scene.
entries.definitionCN: 视力或宏大的未来设想；它不是有意识地想象某个场景的动作。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning able to be seen; visualizing may produce something visible, but the words are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为能被看见；视觉化可以产生可见之物，但两者不能互换。

entries.definition: To form an idea or picture in the mind; it is broader than visualize, which insists on a visual form.
entries.definitionCN: 在脑中形成观念或画面；它比 visualize 更宽，后者坚持视觉形式。

entries.definition: To picture something as a future possibility; it often carries a sense of planning or hope.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物想象为未来的可能；常带规划或希望意味。

entries.definition: To form a mental image, especially a vivid one; it is the plain equivalent of visualize in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 形成心理图像，尤指鲜明图像；在口语中是 visualize 的朴素对应词。

entries.definition: To perceive with the eyes; the literal sense of visualize is rare, and see remains the ordinary verb.
entries.definitionCN: 用眼睛感知；visualize 的字面义罕见，see 仍是最普通的动词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the sight root, the making suffix and the athlete who runs the race twice.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「看见」词根、表示「使成为」的后缀，以及把赛程跑两遍的运动员。

normal.en: The word is visual plus a suffix that means to make: to make a picture where there was none.
normal.cn: 这个词是 visual 加表示「使成为」的后缀：在原本没有画面的地方造出画面。

normal.en: The family runs visual, visualize, visualization, visually and visualizer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 visual、visualize、visualization、visually 与 visualizer。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show its two homes: visualize data in computing, visualize a scene in the mind.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示它的两个归属：计算中的把数据可视化，心智中的想象场景。

normal.en: Athletes use the verb for rehearsal: they visualize the turns before the gun fires.
normal.cn: 运动员用这个动词指预演：发令枪响之前先想象弯道。

normal.en: The same Latin root appears in vision, visible, visibility and video-like words.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁词根还出现在 vision、visible、visibility 等词中。

abstract.en: Picture a blank page that already holds a finished building, faint but complete.
abstract.cn: 想象一张空白纸，上面已经有一栋完成的建筑，淡淡的却完整。

abstract.en: Picture a runner who crosses the finish line before the race begins.
abstract.cn: 想象一个跑者在比赛开始之前先冲过一次终点线。

abstract.en: Picture numbers climbing out of a spreadsheet and arranging themselves into a graph.
abstract.cn: 想象数字从表格里爬出来，自己排成一张图。

examples.en: Try to visualize the room before you move any furniture.
examples.cn: 在搬动家具之前，先试着想象这个房间的样子。

examples.en: The software visualizes every route taken by the delivery vans.
examples.cn: 这个软件把配送车走过的每条路线都可视化。

examples.en: Patients who visualize recovery often stick to rehabilitation longer.
examples.cn: 想象康复过程的病人往往能坚持复健更久。

dict_mnemonic.text: 让眼睛先在脑子里看见，再把那个画面造出来 → 想象、使可视化

root: 拉丁 videre「看见」→ visus「视觉」→ 晚期拉丁 visualis「视觉的」→ 英语 visual；加动词后缀 -ize 成 visualize。videre 更早来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of making visible: the mind pictures what is absent, the designer pictures what is unbuilt, the program pictures what is abstract, and the lecturer pictures it for others.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次「使可见」展开：心智看见不在场之物，设计师看见尚未建成之物，程序看见抽象之物，讲者则替别人把它画出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blank sheet on which a finished object is already faintly visible.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张空白纸上，一件成品已经淡淡地显现。

branches.en: THE INNER PICTURE: what is not here is made present to the mind's eye.
branches.cn: 内心画面：不在场之物被带到心灵之眼前。

branches.en: THE FUTURE: an outcome is pictured before it exists so it can be prepared for.
branches.cn: 未来：结果在存在之前被想象，以便为之准备。

branches.en: THE ABSTRACT: numbers and relations acquire edges on a screen.
branches.cn: 抽象之物：数字与关系在屏幕上获得边缘。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN AND THE FAINT: tissue and traces become visible to the eye.
branches.cn: 隐藏与微弱之物：组织与痕迹变得肉眼可见。

branches.en: THE PLAN AND THE LESSON: the picture guides a maker and then an audience.
branches.cn: 计划与讲授：画面先指引制作者，再指引受众。

intro.en: Visualize is an adjective turned into a verb, and the whole sight family can be read from one Latin root.
intro.cn: visualize 是由形容词转成的动词，整个视觉词族都可以从一个拉丁词根读起。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and its participle visus supply vision, visible, visual and visualize; the English suffixes then extend the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 videre 及其分词 visus 提供 vision、visible、visual 与 visualize；英语后缀再延伸这个词族。

items.example: Every word here descends from this verb.
items.exampleCN: 这里的每个词都源自这个动词。

items.example: The visual effect was immediate.
items.exampleCN: 视觉效果立刻显现。

items.example: She visualized the finished room.
items.exampleCN: 她想象出房间完工的样子。

items.meaning: the act or result of visualizing
items.example: The visualization filled the screen.
items.exampleCN: 可视化图占满屏幕。

items.example: The two layouts are visually similar.
items.exampleCN: 两种版式在视觉上相似。

items.meaning: a tool or person that visualizes
items.meaningCN: 可视化工具；擅长视觉想象的人
items.example: The visualizer updates every second.
items.exampleCN: 这个可视化工具每秒更新。

items.example: Her vision changed the project.
items.exampleCN: 她的远见改变了这个项目。

items.example: The crack is visible from the road.
items.exampleCN: 从路上就能看见那道裂缝。

items.example: They envision a car-free centre.
items.exampleCN: 他们设想一个无车中心区。

derivatives.meaning: having been pictured or made visible

definition_zh: 想象力；想象；幻想；创造力；设想
definition_en: the power of forming pictures and ideas in the mind, especially ones that are not present or not real
core_image: 一间没有窗户的屋子里，孩子用粉笔在地上画出一整片海。
scene: 停电的夜晚，孩子们躺在床上，用同一个旧故事编出完全不同的结局。In the dark, the children used imagination to turn one old story into three different endings.
sceneCN: 这里 imagination 指「在头脑中造出不在眼前之物的能力」（第 1 个义项：形成非现实画面的心理能力）；句意为停电之夜，孩子们凭想象力把同一个旧故事编成三个不同结局。可辨识物件：黑暗的房间、床、旧故事书、孩子。

pos.zh: 想象力；想象；幻想；创造力

forms.label: 形容词（想象中的；虚构的）

senses.title: The power to picture what is absent
senses.titleCN: 造出不在场画面的能力
senses.definition: the mental capacity to form images or ideas of things that are not present to the senses
senses.definitionCN: 对感官不在场的事物形成图像或观念的心理能力
senses.example: In the dark, the children used imagination to turn one old story into three different endings.
senses.exampleCN: 停电的夜里，孩子们凭想象力把同一个旧故事编成三个不同结局。
senses.why: The Latin source is a word for image, so imagination is the mind's image-making power.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的拉丁来源是表示「图像」的词，因此想象就是心智造像的能力。

senses.title: The act of imagining
senses.definition: the activity of forming pictures or scenarios in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 在头脑中形成画面或情境的活动
senses.example: The novel asks for imagination rather than memory.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说需要的是想象，而不是记忆。
senses.why: As an action noun, the word can name the doing as well as the power behind it.
senses.whyCN: 作为动作名词，这个词既可指行为本身，也可指行为背后的能力。

senses.title: Something invented in the mind
senses.definition: a product of the mind that has no counterpart in the external world
senses.definitionCN: 心智的产物，在外部世界没有对应物
senses.example: The monster was a product of his imagination, not of the forest.
senses.exampleCN: 那只怪物是他想象出来的，并非森林里的东西。
senses.why: The noun of power can also name what the power makes, so an imagined thing is an imagination.
senses.whyCN: 表示能力的名词也能指该能力所造之物，因此想象出来的东西也可称为想象。

senses.title: The creative faculty
senses.definition: the ability to produce original ideas, designs or works
senses.definitionCN: 产生原创观念、设计或作品的能力
senses.example: The design shows imagination as well as skill.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计既显示技巧，也显示创造力。
senses.why: Creating something new requires picturing what does not yet exist, so the image-making power becomes a creative one.
senses.whyCN: 创造新事物需要先看见尚不存在之物，因此造像能力也就成为创造能力。

senses.title: Unfounded invention or fancy
senses.definition: an idea or story invented without evidence, often with a hint of suspicion
senses.definitionCN: 没有证据而编造的观念或说法，常带怀疑意味
senses.example: The rumour was pure imagination dressed as evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 那则谣言纯粹是披着证据外衣的臆想。
senses.why: The same power that creates art can also invent what is false, and the word takes on a critical edge.
senses.whyCN: 创造艺术的能力同样能编造虚假之物，这个词因而带上了批评色彩。

senses.title: Picturing a possible future
senses.definition: the act of imagining how things could be, especially as a basis for planning
senses.definitionCN: 想象事物可能的样子，尤作为规划基础
senses.example: The plan began with an imagination of the city in twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划始于对二十年后城市的设想。
senses.why: Planning requires a picture of what is not yet here, which is the forward-looking face of the same power.
senses.whyCN: 规划需要一幅尚不存在之物的画面，这是同一种能力朝前的面向。

senses.title: The ability to enter another's position
senses.titleCN: 设身处地理解他人的能力
senses.definition: the capacity to picture another person's feelings or situation as if from inside
senses.definitionCN: 像从内部一样想象他人感受或处境的能力
senses.example: Reading fiction can strengthen imagination for other lives.
senses.exampleCN: 阅读小说能增强对他人生活的设身处地之能。
senses.why: To imagine someone else is to make a picture of a mind one cannot see, using the same faculty.
senses.whyCN: 想象别人，就是为看不见的心灵造一幅画，用的正是同一种能力。

senses.title: The imaginative side of art
senses.definition: the element in art or writing that goes beyond direct observation and invention of fact
senses.definitionCN: 艺术或写作中超出直接观察与事实记录的部分
senses.example: The painting's imagination lies in its colour, not its subject.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画的想象在于色彩，而不在题材。
senses.why: Art criticism uses the word for the invented layer that distinguishes a work from a record.
senses.whyCN: 艺术评论用这个词指使作品区别于记录的虚构层。

intro.en: Imagination comes from Latin imaginatio, a noun of action from imaginari, to form a picture, itself from imago, an image.
intro.cn: imagination 来自拉丁动作名词 imaginatio，其动词 imaginari 意为「形成图像」，又来自 imago「图像」。

items.en: Imago meant an image, likeness or copy, including the wax mask of a dead ancestor. Its deeper origin is generally considered to involve a reconstructed root, and the exact earlier form is unsettled.
items.cn: imago 指图像、相似物或摹本，也包括死者祖先的蜡制面像。其更早来源一般被认为涉及某个重构词根，确切形态尚无定论。

items.en: Imaginari meant to form an image in the mind or to picture something to oneself, a verb built on the noun for image.
items.cn: imaginari 意为在头脑中形成图像或向自己描绘某物，是由「图像」名词构成的动词。

items.en: The action noun imaginatio named the forming of images, and in later use also the faculty that does it.
items.cn: 动作名词 imaginatio 指形成图像的行为，后来也指执行该行为的能力。

items.en: Old French imagination carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, where it first named the faculty and its products.
items.cn: 古法语 imagination 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语，最初兼指该能力及其产物。

items.en: Psychology and aesthetics gave the word new weight in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, linking it to creativity and to sympathy with others.
items.cn: 心理学与美学在十八、十九世纪赋予这个词新的分量，把它与创造力及对他人的共情联系起来。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin of image): the older source of imago is a reconstructed form, and the exact date when the creative sense became standard is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（「图像」义的拉丁语之前来源）：imago 的更早来源属重构形式；创造义成为标准用法的确切年代亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds family adjectives that are constantly confused; group two holds near names for the inventive power.
note.cn: 第一组是同族中极易混淆的形容词；第二组是表示「创造能力」的近义词。

entries.definition: Describing a person or work that shows imagination; it is a compliment, not a claim that something is unreal.
entries.definitionCN: 描述人或作品富有想象；它是褒义，而非声称某物不真实。

entries.definition: Existing only in the mind; an imaginary friend is not real, while an imaginative friend is full of ideas.
entries.definitionCN: 只存在于心中；想象中的朋友并不真实，而富有想象力的朋友满脑子点子。

entries.definition: Able to be imagined; it describes possibility, not creative strength.
entries.definitionCN: 可以被想象到的；它描述可能性，而非创造力。

entries.definition: A visible representation or a picture in the mind; imagination is the power that makes such images.
entries.definitionCN: 可见的再现物或心中画面；想象力是制造这些图像的能力。

entries.definition: The ability to produce original works or ideas; it stresses output, while imagination stresses the inner picture.
entries.definitionCN: 产生原创作品或观念的能力；它强调产出，而 imagination 强调内心画面。

entries.definition: A imagined scene, often pleasant and unlikely; it is one product of imagination, not the power itself.
entries.definitionCN: 想象出的场景，常为愉悦而不太可能；它是想象的一种产物，而非能力本身。

entries.definition: Something new that has been made or made up; invention is the result, imagination the capacity behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 新造出或编造出的东西；发明是结果，想象力是背后的能力。

entries.definition: A large picture of what could be; it is a forward-looking product of imagination, often shared with others.
entries.definitionCN: 对未来可能之事的宏大画面；它是想象朝前的产物，常与他人共享。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the image root, the four family adjectives and the child in the dark room.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「图像」词根、四个同族形容词，以及黑暗房间里的孩子。

normal.en: The Latin source means image: imagination is the mind's power to make images.
normal.cn: 拉丁来源意为「图像」：想象就是心智制造图像的能力。

normal.en: The family runs imagine, imagination, imaginative, imaginary, imaginable and unimaginable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 imagine、imagination、imaginative、imaginary、imaginable 与 unimaginable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its force: capture the imagination, a vivid imagination, a figment of the imagination.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出它的力量：激发想象、丰富的想象力、想象出来的虚构之物。

normal.en: The noun covers both the power and its products, so one word names the ability and the invented thing.
normal.cn: 这个名词兼指能力与产物，因此同一个词既指才能，也指编造出来的东西。

normal.en: The same root appears in image, imagery and imagine, all tied to pictures.
normal.cn: 同一词根还出现在 image、imagery 与 imagine 中，都与画面有关。

abstract.en: Picture a windowless room where a child draws a whole sea on the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一间没有窗户的屋子，孩子在地上画出一整片海。

abstract.en: Picture a blank map that fills itself with countries no one has visited.
abstract.cn: 想象一张空白地图自己长出无人到过的国家。

abstract.en: Picture a story that changes its ending each time it is told.
abstract.cn: 想象一个故事，每讲一次就换一个结局。

examples.en: The plan failed for lack of imagination, not lack of money.
examples.cn: 这项计划失败是因为缺乏想象力，而非缺钱。

examples.en: Her imagination made the empty stage feel like a forest.
examples.cn: 她的想象让空荡的舞台像一片森林。

examples.en: It takes imagination to see a use for something everyone else discards.
examples.cn: 要看出别人都丢弃的东西有什么用途，需要想象力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 在脑子里造出一张并不存在的画面，并让它活起来 → 想象、想象力

root: 拉丁 imago「图像、相似物」（词干 imagin-）→ 动词 imaginari「形成图像」→ 动作名词 imaginatio；经古法语 imagination 入英语。imago 更早来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image-making: the mind forms a picture of what is absent, and that power becomes an act, a product, a creative force, a false story, a future plan, a way into others and the invented layer of art.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次造像展开：心智为不在场之物造出画面；这种能力随后成为行为、产物、创造力、虚假故事、未来设想、进入他人处境的方式，以及艺术中的虚构层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child drawing a sea on the floor of a room with no window.
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子在无窗房间的地板上画出一片海。

branches.en: THE POWER AND THE ACT: the capacity and its exercise are named by one word.
branches.cn: 能力与行为：才能与它的运用由同一个词命名。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT: what is pictured can stand in the room as if it were real.
branches.cn: 产物：被想象之物可以像真的那样站在房间里。

branches.en: THE CREATIVE LAYER: new works and the invented part of art come from the same source.
branches.cn: 创造层：新作品与艺术中的虚构部分来自同一个源头。

branches.en: THE FALSE PICTURE: the same power can dress a rumour as evidence.
branches.cn: 虚假画面：同一种能力能把谣言装扮成证据。

branches.en: THE FUTURE AND THE OTHER: the picture can point at what may be or at what someone else feels.
branches.cn: 未来与他人：画面可以指向可能之事，也可以指向他人感受。

intro.en: Imagination is a Latin action noun from a word for image, and its family splits into adjectives that are easy to confuse.
intro.cn: imagination 是来自「图像」一词的拉丁动作名词，其词族分成几个容易混淆的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin imago, imaginari and imaginatio supply image, imagine, imagination, imaginary and imaginative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 imago、imaginari 与 imaginatio 提供 image、imagine、imagination、imaginary 与 imaginative。

items.example: The image stayed with her for years.
items.exampleCN: 那幅画面在她心中留了很多年。

items.meaning: to form a picture in the mind
items.example: Imagine a room with no doors.
items.exampleCN: 想象一个没有门的房间。

items.meaning: the power or act of picturing
items.example: Imagination needs no permission.
items.exampleCN: 想象不需要许可。

items.example: The solution was imaginative and cheap.
items.exampleCN: 这个解决办法既富想象又便宜。

items.meaningCN: 只存在于心中的；虚构的
items.example: The line on the map is imaginary.
items.exampleCN: 地图上的那条线是虚构的。

items.example: Every imaginable colour was used.
items.exampleCN: 每一种能想到的颜色都用上了。

items.example: The heat was unimaginable.
items.exampleCN: 那种炎热难以想象。

items.meaning: images as a group, especially in art or writing
items.meaningCN: 图像的总称，尤指艺术或文学中的意象
items.example: The poem's imagery is drawn from the sea.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗的意象取自大海。

items.example: The study measured imaginational fluency.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究测量想象的流畅度。

derivatives.meaning: relating to images in the mind

latinEntries.structure: imaginari, imaginatus sum (verb, first conjugation, deponent)

definition_zh: 富有想象力的；有创造性的；虚构的；善于构想的
definition_en: showing or having a lively imagination, especially in making new ideas or works
core_image: 一把普通椅子被孩子改造成飞船，扶手上挂着纸做的控制杆。
scene: 美术课上，一个学生把废旧纸箱剪成城市、桥梁和会转的风车。Her imaginative model turned a cardboard box into a city with bridges and windmills.
sceneCN: 这里 imaginative 指「显示出丰富想象力的」（第 1 个义项：作品或人具备活跃的造像能力）；句意为她富有想象力的模型把纸箱变成带桥梁与风车的城市。可辨识物件：纸箱、剪刀、桥梁、风车、课桌。

pos.zh: 富有想象力的；有创造性的；虚构的

senses.title: Full of imagination
senses.definition: showing a lively power to form new pictures and ideas
senses.definitionCN: 显示出活跃的造像与构思能力
senses.example: Her imaginative model turned a cardboard box into a city with bridges and windmills.
senses.exampleCN: 她富有想象力的模型把纸箱变成带桥梁与风车的城市。
senses.why: The adjective adds a suffix meaning tending to, so it describes whatever tends to produce imagination.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词加上表示「倾向于」的后缀，因此描述倾向于产生想象的人或物。

senses.title: Creative in method
senses.definition: using original ideas rather than repeating a known procedure
senses.definitionCN: 采用原创观念，而非重复已知程序
senses.example: The team found an imaginative way to reuse the old pipes.
senses.exampleCN: 团队找到一种有创意的办法来再利用旧管道。
senses.why: Creativity and imagination overlap here: a new method must be pictured before it can be tried.
senses.whyCN: 创造与想象在此重叠：新方法必须先被想象出来，才谈得上尝试。

senses.title: Existing only in the mind
senses.titleCN: 虚构的；只存在于想象中的
senses.definition: describing something invented by the mind rather than observed in the world
senses.definitionCN: 描述由心智编造、而非在现实中观察到的某物
senses.example: The story takes place in an imaginative kingdom with two moons.
senses.exampleCN: 故事发生在一个有两轮月亮的想象王国里。
senses.why: An invented world is a product of imagination, so works that build one are called imaginative.
senses.whyCN: 虚构世界是想象的产物，因此构建这类世界的作品被称为富有想象力的。

senses.title: Good at devising new options
senses.definition: able to think of fresh possibilities when the obvious ones fail
senses.definitionCN: 在显而易见的办法失效时能想出新的可能
senses.example: An imaginative manager sees three uses for a dead afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 一位善于构想的经理能从一个空闲的下午看出三种用途。
senses.why: The trait is applied to people, not works, when the point is the ability to keep generating options.
senses.whyCN: 当重点在于不断产生选项的能力时，这个词用于人，而非作品。

senses.title: Vivid and engaging in description
senses.titleCN: 描写生动的、引人入胜的
senses.definition: presenting something in a way that lets a reader picture it strongly
senses.definitionCN: 以让读者强烈想象到的方式呈现某物
senses.example: The guide gave an imaginative account of the market's smells.
senses.exampleCN: 向导对市场的气味作了生动的描述。
senses.why: A description can lend the reader another person's imagination, so the adjective moves from maker to text.
senses.whyCN: 描写能把作者的想象借给读者，因此这个形容词从创作者转到文本。

senses.title: Forward-looking in planning
senses.definition: able to picture a future state and plan toward it
senses.definitionCN: 能够想象未来状态并据此规划
senses.example: The proposal was imaginative enough to survive three budget cuts.
senses.exampleCN: 这项提案足够有远见，历经三次预算削减仍保留下来。
senses.why: Planning needs an image of what does not exist yet, which is imagination put to practical use.
senses.whyCN: 规划需要尚不存在之物的画面，这是想象投入实际用途。

senses.title: Prone to fancy
senses.definition: habitually turning to invented scenes or stories, sometimes at the cost of practical attention
senses.definitionCN: 习惯性转向虚构场景或故事，有时以实际注意力为代价
senses.example: The imaginative child missed the bell, still inside a story.
senses.exampleCN: 那个爱幻想的孩子还待在故事里，没听见铃声。
senses.why: The same tendency has a distracted side, so the adjective can describe someone lost in invented scenes.
senses.whyCN: 同一种倾向也有分神的一面，因此这个形容词可描述沉入虚构场景的人。

senses.title: Belonging to imaginative art
senses.definition: relating to art or writing whose value lies in invention rather than factual record
senses.definitionCN: 指价值在于创造而非事实记录的艺术或写作
senses.example: The course separates imaginative writing from reportage.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程把想象性写作与报道写作分开。
senses.why: Schools label a whole domain by the faculty it exercises, so fiction and poetry become imaginative writing.
senses.whyCN: 学校用所运用的能力来命名整个领域，于是小说与诗歌成为想象性写作。

intro.en: Imaginative comes from Late Latin imaginativus, an adjective built on imaginatio, imagination, and reached English through French.
intro.cn: imaginative 来自晚期拉丁形容词 imaginativus，建立在 imaginatio「想象」之上，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Imago meant an image or likeness. Its deeper origin is generally considered to involve a reconstructed root, and the exact earlier form is not settled.
items.cn: imago 指图像或相似物。其更早来源一般被认为涉及某个重构词根，确切更早形态尚无定论。

items.en: Imaginari meant to form an image in the mind, a verb built on the noun for image.
items.cn: imaginari 意为在头脑中形成图像，是由「图像」名词构成的动词。

items.en: The adjective imaginativus described what belongs to the image-forming power, and it is the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: 形容词 imaginativus 描述属于造像能力的事物，是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French imaginatif carried the adjective into English in the fourteenth century, alongside imagination and imagine.
items.cn: 古法语 imaginatif 在十四世纪把这个形容词带入英语，与 imagination、imagine 同时进入。

items.en: English later divided the family: imaginative describes creative power, imaginary describes what is not real, and imaginable describes what can be pictured.
items.cn: 英语后来把这个词族分工：imaginative 描述创造能力，imaginary 描述不真实之物，imaginable 描述可被想象之物。

items.en: Source uncertain (first English date and pre-Latin origin of image): the earliest citation is not firmly fixed, and the deeper source of imago is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英语首见年代与「图像」义的拉丁语之前来源）：最早书证没有定论；imago 的更早来源属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the three adjectives that English speakers most often mix up; group two holds near words for creative strength.
note.cn: 第一组是英语使用者最常混淆的三个形容词；第二组是表示创造能力的近义词。

entries.definition: Existing only in the mind; an imaginary country is invented, but the adjective says nothing about whether the invention is good.
entries.definitionCN: 只存在于心中；想象中的国度是虚构的，但这个形容词并不评价虚构得好不好。

entries.definition: Able to be imagined; it marks the limit of possibility, as in every imaginable colour.
entries.definitionCN: 能被想象到的；它标出可能性的边界，如每一种想得到的颜色。

entries.definition: The power or its products; imaginative is the adjective describing someone or something that has it.
entries.definitionCN: 能力或其产物；imaginative 是描述拥有该能力的人或物的形容词。

entries.definition: A visible or mental picture; imaginative work is full of images, but the two words are different parts of speech.
entries.definitionCN: 可见或心中的画面；富有想象力的作品充满画面，但这两个词词性不同。

entries.definition: Producing original works or ideas; imaginative stresses the inner picture, creative stresses the output.
entries.definitionCN: 产生原创作品或观念；imaginative 强调内心画面，creative 强调产出。

entries.definition: Skilled at inventing devices or solutions; it is close to imaginative but often more practical.
entries.definitionCN: 擅长发明装置或办法；与 imaginative 相近，但通常更务实。
