entries.definition: New and not derived from something else; an original idea may or may not be imaginative in style.
entries.definitionCN: 新的、并非来自他物的；原创观念未必在风格上富有想象。

entries.definition: Guided by fancy rather than reason, often in a playful or unrealistic way.
entries.definitionCN: 受幻想而非理性引导，常带玩闹或不切实际意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the image root, the tending-to suffix and the three adjectives that split the family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「图像」词根、表示「倾向于」的后缀，以及把这个词族分开的三个形容词。

normal.en: The word is imagination plus a suffix meaning tending to: tending to make images.
normal.cn: 这个词是 imagination 加表示「倾向于」的后缀：倾向于造像。

normal.en: The family split three ways: imaginative means creative, imaginary means unreal, imaginable means possible to picture.
normal.cn: 这个词族分成三支：imaginative 指有创造力，imaginary 指不真实，imaginable 指可以被想象。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its uses: imaginative writing, an imaginative solution, an imaginative child.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：想象性写作、有创意的解决办法、想象力丰富的孩子。

normal.en: The same root appears in image, imagery and imagine, all concerned with pictures.
normal.cn: 同一词根还出现在 image、imagery 与 imagine 中，都与画面有关。

normal.en: A cardboard box turned into a city is the adjective made visible.
normal.cn: 一只纸箱变成一座城市，就是这个形容词的可见形态。

abstract.en: Picture a chair that has quietly become a spaceship without losing its legs.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子悄悄变成飞船，却没有失去它的腿。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase that turns into a river when no one is watching.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯在无人注意时变成一条河。

abstract.en: Picture a lesson plan that folds itself into a paper bird and flies.
abstract.cn: 想象一份教案把自己折成纸鸟飞走。

examples.en: The most imaginative answer was also the cheapest.
examples.cn: 最有想象力的答案同时也是最便宜的。

examples.en: Her imaginative staging used only shadows and one lamp.
examples.cn: 她的舞台设计富有想象，只用影子与一盏灯。

examples.en: Children are often more imaginative with a plain box than with a finished toy.
examples.cn: 孩子面对一个普通纸箱，往往比面对一件成品玩具更有想象力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 脑子里装满画面，随手就能把旧东西想成新东西 → 富有想象力的

root: 拉丁 imago「图像」→ imaginari「形成图像」→ imaginatio「想象」→ 晚期拉丁 imaginativus；经法语 imaginatif 入英语为 imaginative。imago 更早来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one tendency: a person or work tends to make images, and that tendency shows as creative method, invented worlds, practical resourcefulness, vivid description, foresight, daydreaming and a whole artistic domain.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种倾向展开：人或作品倾向于造像，这种倾向表现为有创意的方法、虚构世界、务实的机变、生动的描写、远见、白日梦以及整个艺术领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an ordinary chair wearing paper wings and a cardboard control stick.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把普通椅子装上纸翅膀和纸板操纵杆。

branches.en: THE TRAIT: the base sense is simply a lively image-making tendency.
branches.cn: 特质：基础义就是活跃的造像倾向。

branches.en: THE METHOD: new procedures and fresh options are pictured before they are tried.
branches.cn: 方法：新程序与新选项在尝试之前先被想象出来。

branches.en: THE INVENTED WORLD: fiction and imaginative art live in pictures of what is not.
branches.cn: 虚构世界：小说与想象性艺术活在「不存在之物」的画面里。

branches.en: THE DESCRIPTION: a text can lend its pictures to a reader.
branches.cn: 描写：文本可以把它的画面借给读者。

branches.en: THE FORWARD AND THE LOST: the same tendency can plan ahead or drift away.
branches.cn: 向前与走神：同一种倾向既能规划未来，也能飘走。

intro.en: Imaginative is an adjective of tendency built on the imagination family, which comes from a Latin word for image.
intro.cn: imaginative 是建立在想象词族之上的倾向形容词，该词族来自拉丁语中表示「图像」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin imago and imaginatio give image, imagine and imagination; the adjective suffix -ive then forms imaginative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 imago 与 imaginatio 提供 image、imagine 与 imagination；形容词后缀再构成 imaginative。

items.example: The image of the sea stayed with her.
items.exampleCN: 大海的画面留在她心里。

items.example: Imagine a city with no cars.
items.exampleCN: 想象一座没有汽车的城市。

items.example: Imagination outruns the budget.
items.exampleCN: 想象跑得比预算快。

items.example: The design is imaginative and simple.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计富有想象又简单。

items.example: The room was imaginatively lit.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间的灯光设计很有想象。

items.example: The sequel was unimaginative.
items.exampleCN: 这部续集缺乏想象力。

items.example: The border is imaginary.
items.exampleCN: 那条边界是虚构的。

items.example: Every imaginable excuse was tried.
items.exampleCN: 每一种想得到的借口都试过了。

items.example: The imagery is drawn from winter.
items.exampleCN: 这些意象取自冬天。

latinEntries.structure: imaginari, imaginatus sum (verb, first conjugation, deponent)

definition_zh: 创造力；创造性；独创性；创作能力
definition_en: the ability to produce original ideas, works or solutions
core_image: 三样毫不相干的物件在孩子手里被拼成一个能站住的新东西。
scene: 工作室的墙上贴满被否掉的草稿，最后留下来的方案把两种旧工具合成了一种新用法。The studio's walls were covered with rejected drafts before creativity produced a new use for two old tools.
sceneCN: 这里 creativity 指「产生原创想法或作品的能力」（第 1 个义项：造出此前不存在之物的总体能力）；句意为墙上贴满被否掉的草稿，最后创造力把两种旧工具合成一种新用法。可辨识物件：草稿墙、旧工具、工作台、最终方案。

forms.label: 复数（少见，指不同形式的创造力）

senses.title: The power to make something new
senses.titleCN: 造出新事物的总体能力
senses.definition: the general ability to produce ideas, works or solutions that did not exist before
senses.definitionCN: 产生此前不存在的观念、作品或解决办法的总体能力
senses.example: The studio's walls were covered with rejected drafts before creativity produced a new use for two old tools.
senses.exampleCN: 墙上贴满被否掉的草稿，最后创造力把两种旧工具合成一种新用法。
senses.why: The noun is built on create, so it names the power behind making something that was not there.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词建立在「创造」之上，因此指造出原本不存在之物的能力。

senses.title: The quality of being creative
senses.definition: the degree to which an idea or work shows original invention
senses.definitionCN: 一个观念或作品显示原创发明的程度
senses.example: Judges scored the entries for creativity rather than polish.
senses.exampleCN: 评委按创造性而非完成度给参赛作品打分。
senses.why: The abstract noun can name a measurable quality, which is how competitions and schools use it.
senses.whyCN: 抽象名词可以指一种可测量的性质，比赛与学校正是这样使用它。

senses.title: Originality that stands apart
senses.definition: the quality of being unlike what already exists, especially in a striking way
senses.definitionCN: 与既有之物不同、尤指以显著方式不同的性质
senses.example: The building's creativity lies in what it leaves out.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑的独创性在于它省略了什么。
senses.why: Newness alone is not enough; the word often implies a difference that others can recognize.
senses.whyCN: 单纯的新还不够；这个词常暗示一种别人能认出的差异。

senses.title: The artist's working power
senses.definition: the capacity to invent and shape works in a medium such as paint, sound or words
senses.definitionCN: 在绘画、声音或文字等媒介中发明并塑造作品的能力
senses.example: Her creativity shows most clearly in small drawings.
senses.exampleCN: 她的创作能力在小幅画作中最清楚。
senses.why: Art gives the power a medium, so creativity becomes the ability to shape material into a new form.
senses.whyCN: 艺术给这种能力一个媒介，于是创造力成为把材料塑成新形式的本领。

senses.title: Creativity shared by a group
senses.definition: the combined ability of a group to generate and develop new ideas
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体产生并发展新观念的综合能力
senses.example: Team creativity improved when the quiet members spoke first.
senses.exampleCN: 当沉默的成员先发言时，团队创造力提高了。
senses.why: Organizations treat creativity as a group resource, so the noun is used for a collective rather than one mind.
senses.whyCN: 组织把创造力当作群体资源，因此这个名词用于集体，而非单个头脑。

senses.title: Creative thinking as a process
senses.titleCN: 作为过程的创造性思维
senses.definition: the process of generating, combining and testing novel ideas
senses.definitionCN: 产生、组合并检验新颖观念的过程
senses.example: Creativity is often a loop of making and discarding.
senses.exampleCN: 创造力常常是一个制作与丢弃的循环。
senses.why: The noun can name the activity itself, including its failures, not only the final ability.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词可以指活动本身，包括其中的失败，而不只是最终能力。

senses.title: A period or burst of invention
senses.definition: a stretch of time in which a person or group produces an unusual amount of new work
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或群体产出异常多新作品的一段时间
senses.example: The letters record a burst of creativity before the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这些信件记录了战前一次创造力的迸发。
senses.why: Creativity is uneven, so the word also names its high periods rather than a steady trait.
senses.whyCN: 创造力并不均匀，因此这个词也指它的高峰期，而非稳定特质。

senses.title: Inventiveness in a field
senses.titleCN: 某一领域中的创造能力
senses.definition: the ability to make original contributions within a particular discipline, such as science or business
senses.definitionCN: 在某一特定学科、如科学或商业中作出原创贡献的能力
senses.example: Scientific creativity often looks like a better question, not a louder answer.
senses.exampleCN: 科学创造力常常表现为更好的问题，而不是更响亮的答案。
senses.why: Each field defines what counts as new, so the word takes on the standards of that discipline.
senses.whyCN: 每个领域都定义什么才算新，因此这个词会带上该学科的标准。

intro.en: Creativity is an English noun formed from creative, which comes from create, from Latin creare, to make or bring forth.
intro.cn: creativity 是由 creative 构成的英语名词；creative 来自 create，而 create 来自拉丁 creare「制造、产生」。

items.en: Creare meant to make, bring forth or produce, and was used of gods, parents and makers alike. Its deeper origin is generally considered to involve a reconstructed root, and the exact earlier form is not settled.
items.cn: creare 意为制造、产生或产出，可用于神、父母与制作者。其更早来源一般被认为涉及某个重构词根，确切更早形态尚无定论。

items.en: The action noun creatio named the making, and in Christian writing it became the word for the creation of the world.
items.cn: 动作名词 creatio 指制造行为；在基督教写作中，它成为「创世」一词。

items.en: English create entered in the fifteenth century through French, first in the sense of bringing something into existence.
items.cn: 英语 create 在十五世纪经法语进入，最初指使某物存在。

items.en: Creative added the adjective suffix to create in the seventeenth century; for a long time it described a divine or artistic making.
items.cn: creative 在十七世纪由 create 加形容词后缀而成；很长时间里它描述神圣或艺术的创造。

items.en: Creativity appeared as a noun in the nineteenth century, and psychology made it a measurable subject in the twentieth.
items.cn: creativity 在十九世纪作为名词出现，心理学在二十世纪把它变成可测量的研究对象。

items.en: Source uncertain (first recorded use of creativity and pre-Latin origin of make): the earliest English citation of the noun is not firmly dated, and the deeper source of creare is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（该名词首次记录与「制造」义的拉丁语之前来源）：creativity 最早的英语书证没有确切年代；creare 的更早来源属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the making family that are easy to confuse; group two holds near names for inventive power.
note.cn: 第一组是「制造」词族中容易混淆的词；第二组是表示创造能力的近义词。

entries.definition: The act of making something, or the thing made; creativity is the ability behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 制造某物的动作，或被造之物；creativity 是背后的能力。

entries.definition: A person who makes something; the maker is not the power that the maker uses.
entries.definitionCN: 制造某物的人；制造者并不等于他所运用的能力。

entries.definition: Having the power to create; creativity is the noun for that power.
entries.definitionCN: 具有创造能力的；creativity 是这种能力的名词。

entries.definition: The producing of offspring, from a prefix meaning for or forward plus creare; it is not the same as artistic creativity.
entries.definitionCN: 生育后代，由表示「为了、向前」的前缀加 creare 构成；与艺术创造力不同。

entries.definition: The power to picture what is absent or unreal; creativity puts such pictures into works.
entries.definitionCN: 想象不在场或不真实之物的能力；创造力把这类画面变成作品。

entries.definition: A new method or product, especially one that is put into use; innovation stresses adoption, creativity the making.
entries.definitionCN: 新的方法或产品，尤其指被投入使用的；innovation 强调采用，creativity 强调制造。

entries.definition: The quality of being unlike others; originality is one face of creativity, but creativity also covers usefulness and process.
entries.definitionCN: 与众不同的性质；独创性是创造力的一个面向，但创造力也涵盖实用性与过程。

entries.definition: Something new that has been devised; invention is the product, creativity the capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 被设计出的新东西；发明是产物，创造力是能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the make root, the noun chain from create to creativity, and the wall of rejected drafts.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「制造」词根、从 create 到 creativity 的名词链，以及贴满被否草稿的墙。

normal.en: The Latin verb means to make or bring forth; the noun chain runs create, creative, creativity.
normal.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为制造或产生；名词链依次是 create、creative、creativity。

normal.en: The family runs create, creation, creative, creator, creativity and creatively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 create、creation、creative、creator、creativity 与 creatively。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: artistic creativity, team creativity, creativity research.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：艺术创造力、团队创造力、创造力研究。

normal.en: The word names a capacity, a quality and a period: a person has it, a work shows it, a year can be one.
normal.cn: 这个词兼指能力、性质与时期：人有它，作品显示它，某一年也可以是它。

normal.en: Rejected drafts are part of the word: creativity is often a loop of making and discarding.
normal.cn: 被否掉的草稿也是这个词的一部分：创造力常常是制作与丢弃的循环。

abstract.en: Picture three unrelated objects lying together until a child joins them into something that stands.
abstract.cn: 想象三件毫不相干的物件躺在一起，直到孩子把它们拼成一个能站住的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of crossed-out drawings with one clean sheet at the end.
abstract.cn: 想象一面画满又被划掉的墙，尽头只剩一张干净的纸。

abstract.en: Picture a seed that becomes a tree no one had planted before.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子长成一棵从前无人种过的树。

examples.en: The workshop was designed to give employees time for creativity.
examples.cn: 这个工作坊的设计是为了给员工留出发挥创造力的时间。

examples.en: Creativity rarely appears on a schedule, but it can be given room.
examples.cn: 创造力很少按日程出现，但可以给它空间。

examples.en: Her creativity turned a broken bicycle into a garden cart.
examples.cn: 她的创造力把一辆坏自行车改成了园艺推车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把没有关系的东西拼成一个站得住的新东西 → 创造力

root: 拉丁 creare「制造、产生」→ 动作名词 creatio → 英语 create；加形容词后缀成 creative，再加抽象名词后缀成 creativity。creare 更早来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one making: something new is brought into being, and the same power is read as a quality, an originality, an artistic skill, a group resource, a process, a burst and a field-specific contribution.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次制造展开：新事物被带入存在；同一种能力随后被读作性质、独创性、艺术技艺、群体资源、过程、迸发期以及特定领域的贡献。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three unrelated objects joined into one new thing that can stand.
core.cn: 核心意象：三件毫不相干的物件被拼成一个能站住的新东西。

branches.en: THE POWER AND THE PROCESS: the ability and the loop of making are both named.
branches.cn: 能力与过程：能力本身与制作循环都可用这个词指称。

branches.en: THE QUALITY: a work can be scored for newness and for difference.
branches.cn: 性质：作品可以按新颖度与差异度被打分。

branches.en: THE MEDIUM: paint, sound and words give the power a body.
branches.cn: 媒介：绘画、声音与文字给这种能力一个身体。

branches.en: THE GROUP AND THE MOMENT: creativity can belong to a team or to a season.
branches.cn: 群体与时刻：创造力可以属于一个团队，也可以属于一个时期。

branches.en: THE FIELD: each discipline decides what counts as a new contribution.
branches.cn: 领域：每个学科自己决定什么算新的贡献。

intro.en: Creativity is the end of a short Latin chain: a verb of making becomes a noun, an adjective and finally an abstract noun of ability.
intro.cn: creativity 是一条简短拉丁链的末端：制造动词先成名词，再成形容词，最后成为表示能力的抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin creare gives create, creation, creator, creative and creativity; the suffixes -ive and -ity carry the chain forward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 creare 衍生 create、creation、creator、creative 与 creativity；形容词与抽象名词后缀推动这条链向前。

items.example: The team created a new map.
items.exampleCN: 团队创造了一张新地图。

items.meaning: the act of making or the thing made
items.example: The creation took three years.
items.exampleCN: 这件作品的创作花了三年。

items.example: The creator left the ending open.
items.exampleCN: 创作者把结局留成开放。

items.example: The creative team met on Mondays.
items.exampleCN: 创意团队每周一开会。

items.example: Creativity needs both time and waste.
items.exampleCN: 创造力既需要时间，也需要浪费。

items.example: The room was creatively divided.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间被很有创意地分隔开。

items.example: The uncreative solution copied last year's plan.
items.exampleCN: 这个缺乏创意的方案照抄了去年的计划。
